claim: Scott: the dominant form of subordinate-class action is everyday, low-coordination, individual self-help resistance. Examples are foot dragging, dissimulation, desertion, pilfering and slander. It avoids symbolic confrontation, and Scott judges it often the most effective over the long run.
game_relevance: A group's choice set needs a low-risk, covert tier (slow work, quit, withhold, evade) as well as open action such as join, strike or vote. Most group-periods should resolve in that tier, and the player should see it only as aggregate pressure.

claim: Scott: the form resistance takes depends on the existing form of labor control and on beliefs about retaliation. Piece-work, wages and day-work each generate their own characteristic quiet resistance. Where an open strike risks dismissal or jail, slowdowns replace it.
game_relevance: The choice a group faces is set by its material relation to the employer and the state: wage, piece, tenant or reserve. Open versus covert action is therefore derived from the group's account structure and the repression it expects, not from a fixed disposition.

claim: Weinstein: the risk and delay of payoff set who joins. Where participation is risky and gains are distant, groups attract committed investors (activists). Where it is safe and rewarded immediately, they attract consumers (opportunists). game_relevance: An organization's own endowments (cash, patronage, shared ties) decide what kind of members it attracts, and so how disciplined and durable it is. Bribing recruits with money makes a leaky membership. This is a second source for the ADR184 point that capacity belongs to organizations.

claim: Jackson: a threshold game of strategic complements. A player's best action flips when the number of neighbors acting passes ti. In the special case where benefit scales with neighbors and has fixed cost, ti = ci/ai, so the threshold derives from the player's own cost and benefit.
game_relevance: This gives a threshold that is a result, not an imposed curve. A group's threshold is its own cost divided by the per-contact benefit, both read from its accounts. Cascades then follow from contact structure, not from a response function.

claim: Rank-order under a budget fits the allocation choices of a group. A cohort's period allocates a finite budget (person-hours, or the cash left after the pantry) across a short ranked list of options (look for work, exit, attend, contribute, withhold). The ranking is the net material stake each option offers per hour, with organization presence and repression risk as modifiers. The budget binds, so the lowest-ranked options go unfunded.
game_relevance: This fits Scott's covert-versus-open tiers (CA-01, CA-02) and Kalyvas's ladder (CA-12). It gives mixed outcomes within a class with no sigmoid. Group counts that choose each option sum to cohort counts.

claim: Contact and diffusion can be a finite kernel. Group A's exposure to organization O is the sum, over a finite set of contact hyperedges and adjacent counties, of the share of group members already active there, weighted by shared membership. The kernel has finite support from the county adjacency lookup and uses homophily-weighted membership counts. Thresholds then appear as results when exposure crosses the group's own derived cost-benefit ratio (CA-14).
game_relevance: This turns Jackson-style diffusion into a count-based rule that stays within the rule against a fixed response curve, uses the static adjacency lookup, and keeps community as an overlay, never a graph node.

claim: NORTH_STAR fixes the design envelope. Households are the smallest decision unit and the economy does not simulate individual agents. Class position is how people make a living, who controls their work and who receives its returns. One household can draw wages and ownership income, support a dependent and have someone seeking work. Groups get a distinct part in play 'when they can make a decision of their own'. Residents can share a class position and choose different organizations or decline to join one. Electoral endorsements wait for a working electoral system covering who can vote, what office is at stake and what its holder can decide.
game_relevance: Option 2 (cohort-level bounded choices) matches the text. Two constraints follow. A cohort is not forced to join an organization (a decline option is required), and a household can carry several class-relevant incomes at once, so class position should be a mixture or a dominant source, not a single enum on the household. The electoral system must define the franchise, the office and its powers before any endorsement.
tension: One household drawing wages and ownership income at once conflicts with a single class label per cohort. Any class tag has to be derived from income shares or be allowed to be mixed.

claim: The constitutional rules constrain any decision rule: no rule may impose a sigmoid or a second fixed response curve. Equal inputs must give equal output bytes. A group choice should be a deterministic rank-order or comparison over cohort accounts (for example, rank candidate options by material gain under a budget of hours). It should not be a tuned logistic response or a random draw.
game_relevance: Per-period choices should be argmax/argmin or ordered allocations over material quantities already in the cohort account (hours, cash, unmet need, reserve count), reusing the heat design's rank-order-under-budget pattern. No probabilistic participation rate, no logistic join curve. Any threshold-like outcome must emerge as a result.
tension: A 'join an organization' choice is easy to write as a sigmoid of grievance minus cost. That is exactly what AGENTS.md prohibits. The design has to be a ranking under a time budget.

claim: ADR296 (accepted, Designed, 10 Nov 2026) folds background county contributions into representative principals before actors are built, and says the game 'needs less generated live state'. - IR-04: the 6.5 is a combined average wage factor, not a non-OECD weight.

claim: Cope defines the labour aristocracy as the part of the working class that benefits materially from imperialism and the superexploitation of oppressed-nation workers. Its super-wages let it accumulate savings and invest in property and business, which gives it 'middle-class' status. He defines the proletariat narrowly: it owns no means of production and subsists on wages equal to the value of labour-power. The bourgeoisie includes those who depend on exploitation 'indirectly (through being paid super-wages)'. Class is therefore set by the wage-to-value relation and by asset accrual, not by occupation.
game_relevance: A cohort's class position should be derived from its income streams and asset accrual (wage relative to the value of its labour-power, plus savings and property). It should not be a stored label on the cohort. This fits NORTH_STAR's 'one household can draw wages and ownership income'.

citations.quote: materially from imperialism and the attendant superexploitation of oppressed-nation workers
The super-wages received by the labour aristocracy allow for its accrual of savings and investment in property and business
owns none of the means of production and is forced to subsist entirely upon wages equivalent to the value of labour-power

claim: Cope's operational criterion for the labour aristocracy is a wage-to-value ratio. A worker belongs to it when the wage approaches or exceeds the per capita value created by the working class as a whole. The boundary is stated as 'approaching or exceeding', so it is a fuzzy continuum, not a threshold. For unproductive-sector workers he sets the exploitation test at being paid at or below the per capita value of labour produced by their country.
game_relevance: Classification can be a continuous ratio of wage income per hour to value created per hour, ranked across cohorts. That respects the rule against imposing a threshold constant. It needs the engine's value accounting (value created per labour-hour), so first check whether that exists in the Rust engine.

citations.quote: guarantees its receipt of wages approaching or exceeding the per capita value created by the working class as a whole
may be considered exploited only when they are paid at or below

tension: CONSTITUTION: no imposed sigmoid or fixed response curve. Cope's cutoff is vague, so use it only as a continuous measure or rank order, never as a hard line. The rule against inferring consciousness from provisioning still applies: the ratio gives material position, not belief.

claim: Cope's central estimate is that the OECD workforce (about 600 million) does not generate net profit by itself. His 2009 figures: OECD profits about US$6.8tn, unequal exchange plus capital-export imperialism about US$6.5tn, and about US$500 of profit per OECD worker. He concludes the OECD working class 'receives the full value of its labour' and is a 'bourgeois working class'. He also qualifies this: the work 'does not prove' that OECD productive workers produce no surplus value, only that profits are fully covered by transfers.
game_relevance: These are macro, order-of-magnitude figures from 2008-2010 global data. They can motivate a Designed/Calibrated 'imperial rent share of wage' parameter. They cannot calibrate US county cohorts without a county-level wage-to-value measure.

citations.quote: Value of Unequal Exchange plus Capital Export Imperialism to the OECD in 2009 = US$6.5 trillion
the OECD working class tout court receives the full value of its labour and is, to that extent, a bourgeois working class
the present work does not prove that OECD productive workers do not produce surplus value, it also does not prove that they do

tension: This is the 'whole First World working class' reading of the labour aristocracy. The project's ADR171 (MIM line) splits the US mass into a bribe mass (18.69M persons) and a deprivation mass, in a 1.55x ratio, rather than treating the whole class as aristocratic. See IR-14.
verification_note: All three quotes found at the cited pages. The US$6.8tn (p.220) and the US$500-per-worker figure (p.221) are also in the source. Narrowing: the US$500 figure is a residual (about US$300bn / 600m) that Cope says shows 'some exploitation' of the OECD workforce in 2009 on one measurement, so it is not a flat 'no net profit' result. The tension note's cross-reference to 'IR-14' is wrong: the MIM/ADR171 comparison relates to IR-08 and IR-19, since IR-14 is Mies. ADR171 figures were not re-verified.

claim: Cope's method rests on explicit quantitative assumptions that could be Calibrated inputs. Wage ratio OECD:non-OECD male is 11:1, with a mean wage of US$9.25/h. Underemployment is 17% of OECD workers, each working 862 h/yr, against 1,724 h/yr for the rest and an average of 1,578 h. Non-OECD workers are weighted at about 6.5 average wage factor. One OECD worker 'employs' 1.5 unseen non-OECD producers. Average yearly wage is US$28,536 OECD against US$3,036 non-OECD male.
game_relevance: Gives the shape and magnitude of Calibrated priors: the ratio of paid hours to full-time hours by income quintile (Cope Table III, from Köhler/ILO) and an imperial transfer per core worker. All are global OECD figures, not US-county. The engine's 2080 h/yr full-time constant differs from Cope's 1,724 h OECD average, so unit conversion is needed.

citations.quote: 17% of OECD workers (102 million who are underemployed) each work 862 hours per year
The ratio between OECD and non-OECD male wages is 11:1
for every one OECD worker employed, 1.5 non-OECD producers are working unseen and for free alongside her

verification_note: Quotes found (the 17% quote has a soft-hyphen break 'un- deremployed' in the text layer). 862/1,724/1,578 h, 11:1 and US$9.25 are on p.212; US$28,536 and US$3,036 on p.214 and p.221. claim: Cope says the labour aristocracy is not a passive beneficiary. Because it generally does not own major means of production, it secures its super-wages through active support for the social and political institutions of imperialism. He treats that political agency as what justifies calling it 'exploiting'. He also argues that the metropolitan working class has 'struggled to preserve its affluence politically'.
game_relevance: This gives the mechanism for the political choices in option 2: whether a high-wage-to-value cohort backs, withholds from, or defects from organizations that defend the imperial-rent arrangement. The choice is conditional on the cohort's material position, but it is a choice, not an automatic reading of aid or income.

tension: PER-337: never infer political consciousness or agreement from aid or provisioning. A cohort's backing of a delegate must come from an explicit choice rule over its accounts and the organizations' offers, not from its wage-to-value ratio alone.

claim: Cope's treatment of the US shows the OECD average hides internal colonies. He states he is 'abstracting' from institutional discrimination against minorities and immigrants when he calls the whole OECD working class aristocratic. In Part IV he then argues that US settlerism, mob violence and the systematic oppression of Blacks, Mexicans and Asians underwrote the white working class's 'American lifestyle', and that superexploited internal populations let the US avoid fascism in the 1930s.

claim: Cope's account of fascism: the US, Britain and France used superprofits from colonial, neocolonial and internal-colonial spheres 'to purchase social peace', while Germany lacked such reserves. Fascism 'offers higher wages and living standards to the national workforce at the expense of foreign and colonised workers'. Super-wages therefore contain class struggle while reserves last, and nationalism fills the gap when they fail.
game_relevance: It supports a design in which the sign and size of a cohort's wage-to-value balance feed the fascism-versus-revolution choice, and in which losing the imperial reserve is a trigger for organizational recruitment shifts. It says nothing about thresholds, so keep the response rank-ordered under a budget.

citations.quote: could use the superprofits obtained from their colonial, neocolonial and internal-colonial spheres of influence to purchase social peace

tension: Project memory (re-verify) holds that a positive balance redirects political energy toward chauvinist/fascist forms rather than suppressing it. Cope says superprofits buy 'social peace' and fascism rises where reserves are thin. A reconciliation is possible: peace means no revolutionary choice, and chauvinism is where the energy goes. The two should not be asserted as identical.

claim: Marini defines superexploitation by three mechanisms: intensifying work, extending the working day, and expropriating part of the labour necessary for the worker to replenish labour-power. In each, labour-power is remunerated below its value, because the worker is denied the conditions to replenish labour-power that has been worn away. Smith adds that Marini lets the value of labour-power vary between nations.
game_relevance: Gives a material test for the superexploited position, distinct from the aristocratic one. A cohort is superexploited when its wage plus pantry cannot cover replenishment of its persons' labour-power (including hours worked beyond the normal day). That is checkable from the cohort accounts the engine already holds (cash, pantry, hours).

claim: Osorio (afterword to Marini) identifies appropriation of the worker's consumption fund as the form of superexploitation with the largest effect, and describes the household labour-supply response to it. When the consumption fund is cut, children and adolescents are thrown prematurely into the labour market, and workers accept prolonged working days to get overtime. He also notes superexploitation occurs in the centre too, for certain sectors, particularly migrants, and that sub-value wages drag down average wages even for sectors not directly superexploited.
game_relevance: This is a direct, source-grounded choice rule for the bounded labour-supply decision. A cohort whose pantry or cash falls short of reproduction needs raises labour participation, sending the 16-17 band into work and accepting longer hours. It is also the mechanism for contagion of low wages to other cohorts. It maps onto the lifecycle's existing age bands (under 16, 16-17, 18-64, 65+).

claim: Meillassoux gives the household-as-reproduction-unit argument directly. The hourly wage covers only the worker's maintenance during work time and not his maintenance and reproduction (family, unemployment, illness). Capitalism handles this by splitting direct wage (paid by the employer per hour) from indirect wage (redistributed through a socialised institution according to family situation, children, illness and unemployment). Where only the direct wage is paid, reproduction falls on another mode of production, typically the domestic community.
game_relevance: This maps onto the engine's own accounts: the county public budget's support and grants are the indirect wage, and household pantry plus unpaid hours are the domestic sector. A cohort's class position needs both streams: direct wage from workplaces and indirect wage from the county. Cutting the indirect wage (a county budget decision) is a material class act with consequences for labour supply and organizational choice.

claim: Meillassoux's 'labour rent': a worker employed both in self-sustaining production and in paid work produces labour-rent (the free transfer of labour-power produced in the domestic economy) and surplus-value. Rent is realised pro rata with the hours paid, so it hides inside a cheap wage. Rotating migration keeps the domestic sector bearing reproduction costs, while stabilising migrants raises the cost of labour-power, which gives employers a reason to keep migrants temporary.
game_relevance: A cohort that can self-provision (pantry, garden, kin) lets employers pay below the cost of reproduction. This implies a cohort's reproduction subsidy to employers is measurable as paid wage minus reproduction cost covered by pantry and unpaid hours. It also supplies a reason the 'move county' choice is contested: employers, the state and cohorts have opposed interests in settlement.

claim: Mies defines non-wage subsistence production (mainly women's) as the base on which wage labour becomes 'productive'. She calls the exploitation of non-wage labourers (women, colonies, peasants) superexploitation, because it appropriates the time needed for the person's own survival, not surplus labour time. 'Housewifization' externalizes reproduction costs from capital, and 'proletarianization of men is based on the housewifization of women'.

claim: Proposal: derive each cohort's class mix from three income-stream ratios computed per four-week period. claim: Proposal: derive the bounded household choices from the reproduction-gap logic in IR-10, IR-11 and IR-13. When coverage falls, a cohort may (1) send more of its 16-17 and 65+ persons into the labour force or accept longer paid hours (Osorio), (2) move county, where the indirect wage and reserve competition differ (Meillassoux), and (3) turn to organizations offering relief or bargaining, such as a claimants' assembly. When coverage is high, a cohort's choices are whether to back organizations defending the imperial-rent arrangement (Cope IR-05). A cohort chooses by rank order among the offers available to it, not by a probability curve.
game_relevance: Gives the option-2 choice set a source for each choice and ties each to existing accounts and lifecycle bands. It also gives organizations something concrete to compete over: relief, wages, hours, and the political backing that protects or attacks the indirect wage.

claim: Lawvere (1992) calls the discrete/codiscrete level 'level zero (in itself)', 'often very similar to the category of abstract sets'. Its discrete inclusion often has a further left adjoint, the components functor. Dimension one is the Aufhebung of dimension zero and is characterized through components: if a point can become another, it can do so along a one-dimensional process. In 1994 a discrete space is 'completely deficient in its cohesion', so each point stays itself. A chaotic (codiscrete) space is so excessive in its cohesion that any point moves to any other 'without any effort'. The Hegelian Taco paper adds that one-dimensional figures are the smallest that connect all points that can be connected.

claim: Lawvere (1992) splits variable quantities in two. Extensive quantities are 'quantity of space'; intensive quantities are 'ratios' between extensive ones, as mass and volume are extensive and density intensive. An extensive quantity-type is a covariant coproduct-preserving functor, so it pushes forward and has totals. An intensive type is a contravariant functor taking coproducts to products. Intensives act on extensives (density times volume gives mass), and that action obeys the projection formula, also called Frobenius reciprocity.
game_relevance: Cohort persons, workers, hours, cash and income are extensive and push forward by summation along county → CZ, MSA and state. Rates and shares are intensive and exist only as ratios of extensive sums. The BSL kind law already enforces this.

claim: Mao's 1933 rural classification is explicitly operational. Landlord: owns land, does no or little labour, lives mainly by rent. Rich peasant: labours but relies on exploitation (chiefly hiring labour) for part or most of income. Middle peasant: income wholly or mainly from own labour, generally does not sell labour power. Poor peasant: rents land, is exploited, sells part of its labour power. Worker: owns no or very little land and lives wholly or mainly by selling labour power.
game_relevance: This is a ready template for deriving a class stratum per household cohort from account flows. The inputs are: income share from wages sold, from own-labour production, from hired labour, and from rent, interest and profit; plus ownership. It needs no new primitive, only a classification over existing cohort accounts and company ownership.

The 'afraid of ... a little afraid of the revolution' and 'a lot of faith in its propaganda' wording matches the tension note (the right-wing section is 'a minority'). Claim reworded to attribute 'about one-half' to the middle section accurately.

claim: Mao says the same economic stratum acts differently by period: in normal times the three petty-bourgeois sections differ, but in times of war, when the tide of revolution runs high and victory is in sight, the left-wing joins, the middle section 'may join', and even right-wingers will have to go along. Participation depends on the state of the movement, not only on the stratum.
game_relevance: A cohort's choice should depend on its own accounts plus the visible momentum of the organization or movement (observable strength). That gives bandwagon and waiting behaviour that emerges from material standing and organizational results, with no imposed S-curve. The sigmoid, if any, appears only as a result.

citations.quote: In normal times these three sections of the petty bourgeoisie differ in their attitude to the revolution.
even right-wingers, swept forward by the great revolutionary tide of the proletariat and of the left-wing of the petty bourgeoisie, will have to go along

verification_note: Quotes verified verbatim. Narrowed: the source says the middle section 'may join' (not that it definitely does), and the condition is 'in times of war, that is, when the tide of the revolution runs high and the dawn of victory is in sight'.

claim: The Hunan report is a model of staged group participation. In the first period (membership 300-400k) the rich peasants dismissed the associations (their talk was of Northern Expeditionary Army setbacks). In the second period (membership jumped to two million) the middle peasants joined after the associations 'were already exercising great power', still wanting to wait and see. The poor peasants were the main force throughout; in both periods almost all the chairmen and committee members of the lowest-level associations were poor peasants.
game_relevance: Different strata should join an organization at different points, and joining should depend on that organization's demonstrated power and the cohort's own risk: poor and deficit cohorts first, middle cohorts waiting to see, rich cohorts hostile or withholding. This is directly implementable as a ranking of cohorts by their risk and their material stake, under a budget of organizer capacity, with no threshold constant.

citations.locator: Hunan report, section on the three kinds of peasants (text line ~333-339 of extraction)
citations.quote: It was not until the second period, when the peasant associations were already exercising great power, that the middle peasants came in.
The poor peasants have always been the main force in the bitter fight in the countryside.
Theirs is a vacillating attitude.

verification_note: All quotes found in the local Hunan mirror. 300,000-400,000 and 'jumped to two million' confirmed. 'Supplied almost all the officials' narrowed to what the source says: almost all chairmen and committee members at the lowest-level associations. 'Rich peasants dismissed' is a mild paraphrase of the rich peasants' first-period dismissive talk; the quoted evidence supports the staging, not the word 'dismissed' exactly.

claim: Hunan peasant associations enrolled by household: one name per family, so 2 million members stood for about 10 million people.
game_relevance: This supports the household cohort as the unit of membership. An organization's membership can be a count of cohort-households (with persons attached through the cohort), consistent with NORTH_STAR's household as the smallest decision unit and PER-337's ban on individual person agents. It also warns that membership counts and person counts must be kept apart.

citations.quote: Since the peasants generally enter only one name for the whole family on joining a peasant association, a membership of two million means a mass following of about ten million.

claim: Mao 1957 says 'the people' is a historically variable category, defined by which classes, strata and groups favour or oppose the current task. Contradictions among the people are non-antagonistic and are handled by discussion, criticism, persuasion and education, not coercion. The national bourgeoisie is among the people because of its dual character, although its contradiction with the working class is by nature antagonistic.
game_relevance: Allegiance of a group (people vs enemy) should be a relation recomputed from the current principal task and the group's practice, not a fixed faction flag. The same class can sit in the 'people' camp or outside it as the principal contradiction shifts. The persuasion/coercion distinction also gives two different organization verbs, persuade versus repress, with different effects on members.
tension: Using 'the people' to decide who counts is a reserved theory-line judgment; the engine must derive it from material relations and cannot hard-code it. The 'national bourgeoisie' category is specific to China and may not map to US strata.

citations.quote: The concept of "the people" varies in content in different countries and in different periods of history in a given country.
the classes, strata and social groups which favour, support and work for the cause of socialist construction all come within the category of the people
the democratic method, the method of discussion, criticism, persuasion and education, and not by the method of coercion or repression.

claim: On Contradiction: among many contradictions one is principal; in each contradiction one aspect is principal; the principal contradiction shifts with conditions (for example imperialist invasion relegates internal class contradictions to secondary status for a time). The principal and non-principal aspects transform into each other and their roles are reversed at another stage.
game_relevance: A rank-order design fits. A population group should weigh competing claims on it (employer, landlord, state, organization) by which is currently principal for its accounts, with no fixed weights. Player-facing displays can show 'the principal contradiction here' per county as a derived ranking, which answers a decision question. The reversal of aspects supports a bifurcation modelled as a result and not as a threshold.
tension: Selecting 'the principal contradiction' by a rule is an interpretive step. It must be defined from material quantities (a rank over measured pressures), since the dialectic is primitive and BSL cannot add a mathematical primitive.

citations.locator: section 'The Principal Contradiction and the Principal Aspect of a Contradiction'
citations.quote: one must not treat all the contradictions in a process as being equal but must distinguish between the principal and the secondary contradictions
At such a time, the contradiction between imperialism and the country concerned becomes the principal contradiction

verification_note: Quotes verified. Source wording for the reversal is 'the principal and the non-principal aspects of a contradiction transform themselves into each other ... the roles are reversed', not 'exchange places'; claim reworded accordingly.

claim: Methods of Leadership (1943): masses in any place consist of the relatively active, the intermediate and the relatively backward. Leaders unite the active few and rely on them to raise the level of the intermediate and win over the backward. Correct leadership is 'from the masses, to the masses', an iterated spiral of gathering scattered ideas, concentrating them, returning them as action, and testing them in practice.
game_relevance: This gives the organization-versus-population loop a source: the active, intermediate and backward thirds of a group are a natural three-way split of cohort disposition. The mass line is the player-facing verb loop: listen (read the group's accounts and grievances), concentrate (frame a demand), return (act), then read the result. Its measure of success is observed practice, never player-chosen belief.
tension: The three-part split must be derived from accounts or participation history. A fixed one-third split would be an imposed constant, and the 'empirical invariants' memory notes a one-third/one-third/one-third Pareto pattern, which should not be confused with this.

citations.quote: The masses in any given place are generally composed of three parts, the relatively active, the intermediate and the relatively backward.
all correct leadership is necessarily "from the masses, to the masses".

verification_note: Quotes verified; the 'rely on them to raise the level of the intermediate element and to win over the backward elements' passage is also present. 'Thirds' in game_relevance is the reader's gloss: Mao says three parts, not equal thirds (the tension note already flags this); paragraph locators not independently confirmed.

claim: On Practice makes social practice, including class struggle, the criterion of truth: knowledge is verified only when anticipated results are achieved in practice.
game_relevance: An organization's line must be tested by outcomes, which is the project's stance that direction emerges from practice. Each group's willingness to stay with or leave an organization can be driven by whether the organization's actions delivered on the group's own material accounts, not by a flat 'popularity' scalar.

citations.locator: section on social practice and knowledge
citations.quote: Marxists hold that man's social practice alone is the criterion of the truth of his knowledge of the external world.

claim: Lenin (1916) derives the labour aristocracy from monopoly superprofit: the bourgeoisie spends part of it to bribe its own workers, forming an alliance with its capitalists against other countries. He also says each imperialist power bribes smaller strata of the labour aristocracy than England did in 1848-68 (a 'handful in the top layers'), while the masses are 'more oppressed than before'.
game_relevance: Material basis for a bribed stratum: a cohort whose wage exceeds the value of its labour power is a labour aristocrat in this sense, and its political tendency is toward the bourgeois labour party, not the revolutionary one. This directly supports the project's balance sign and fascism-versus-revolution bifurcation, and it ties the stratum to imperial rent rather than to occupation.
tension: ADR171 gives the project's measured bribe mass (18,691,613 persons, 1.55x the deprivation mass), which makes the bribed stratum far larger than Lenin's 'handful of the top layers'. The reconciliation is the MIM line that this is a whole settler/imperial-country working population and not a thin top layer, so the sources conflict in magnitude and the Director's ruling should govern. Not verified here: whether the ruling's text claims Lenin supports it.

citations.locator: Imperialism and the Split in Socialism
citations.quote: The capitalists can devote a part (and not a small one, at that!) of these superprofits to bribe their own workers
makes it economically possible to bribe the upper strata of the proletariat, and thereby fosters, gives shape to, and strengthens opportunism.

citations.locator: Imperialism and the Split in Socialism, penultimate section
citations.quote: the masses, who are more oppressed than before
bribe mass 18,691,613 persons = 1.55x the deprivation mass (12,041,561)

verification_note: Quotes 1, 2 and 4 verified verbatim (ADR171 lines 24-28 confirmed). The phrase 'oppressed more than before' was wrong: source reads 'more oppressed than before' (the masses 'who are more oppressed than before'); also 'smaller strata (than in England in 1848-68)' and 'bribery of a handful in the top layers' confirmed in the same text. Added the corrected quote as a citation.

claim: Lenin names the political form of the bribed stratum: the 'bourgeois labour party', plus labour ministers, 'labour representatives', labour officials and workers in narrow craft unions. He says this economic fact 'will find political form' and that a bourgeois labour party is 'inevitable and typical in all imperialist countries', though improbable to prevail for long in a number of countries given the struggle for the division of spoils.
game_relevance: An organization type in the game: labour-aristocratic organizations (craft unions, bureaucratised labour parties) that compete with the player for the same cohorts, funded by the superprofit channel. They are rivals for the group's choices, and their appeal rests on the wage premium, not on false belief.

citations.locator: Imperialism and the Split in Socialism
citations.quote: this economic fact, this shift in class relations, will find political form, in one shape or another, without any particular "difficulty".

citations.locator: Imperialism and the Split in Socialism
citations.quote: labour ministers, "labour representatives" (remember Engels's splendid analysis of the term), labour members of War Industries Committees, [5] labour officials, workers belonging to the narrow craft unions

verification_note: Second quote corrected: the source has a footnote marker '[5]' after 'War Industries Committees,' that the reader omitted. Claim corrected: the original said Lenin 'expects it to persist until the revolution'; no such statement exists. Lenin says a bourgeois labour party is 'inevitable and typical in all imperialist countries' but 'improbable that such a party can prevail for long in a number of countries'. The persistence claim was dropped and replaced with what the text states.

claim: Lenin ch.8 names a rentier layer ('people who live by clipping coupons') and says the privileged upper stratum of the proletariat in imperialist countries lives partly at the expense of the oppressed nations. Parasitism and decay are tied to rentiers, export of capital and corruption.
game_relevance: A class-from-accounts classifier needs a rentier income category (coupon, dividend, interest) separate from profit-from-hiring and from wages. Cohorts with mostly property income are a distinct group with distinct choices, for example funding or withholding.

citations.locator: Imperialism and the Split in Socialism, para 1
citations.quote: A privileged upper stratum of the proletariat in the imperialist countries lives partly at the expense of hundreds of millions in the uncivilised nations.
the creation of a huge stratum of rentiers, capitalists who live by "clipping coupons".

claim: WITBD ch.2: the working class by its own effort develops only trade-union consciousness (combine, fight employers, press government for labour legislation); socialist consciousness is brought 'from without'. Lenin adds in a note that bourgeois ideology spontaneously imposes itself upon the working class to a still greater degree than socialism, though socialist theory reveals the causes of workers' misery more correctly than any other theory.
game_relevance: Population groups left to their own accounts will choose economist or trade-union actions (stop looking for work, join a union, back a wage delegate). Political class-consciousness comes only through an organization that does ideological work. This justifies the organization-versus-group structure and a distinct consciousness channel. It also supports the rule that aid or provisioning alone never implies political agreement.
tension: The 'from without' thesis could be read as an exogenous input. Under the compact, consciousness has to arise from material relations and organizational practice inside the model, and a purely scripted 'player injects consciousness' value is a design risk.

citations.locator: ch. II, section on spontaneity of the masses (first section)
citations.quote: the working class, exclusively by its own effort, is able to develop only trade union consciousness
bourgeois ideology spontaneously imposes itself upon the working class to a still greater degree.

verification_note: Quotes verified verbatim. Locator corrected: the second quote is in Lenin's footnote [16] to ch. II (the 'spontaneously gravitates towards socialism' note), with the same sentence also quoted in the chapter text; the 'II(a)' subsection label could not be confirmed. 'Brought from without' confirmed ('introduced into the proletarian class struggle from without').

claim: Left-Wing Communism ch.7: electoral participation is 'obligatory' for the revolutionary party, specifically to educate the backward strata of its own class and the undeveloped rural masses. Participation helps prove to the backward masses why bourgeois parliaments deserve to be done away with.
game_relevance: Elections in the game are an arena for organizational work on backward and intermediate cohorts, not an end in themselves. That matches the player's electoral, reformist or revolutionary options and makes the choice 'back or withhold a delegate' and 'vote' matter as organizing opportunities. It also guards against a pure 'win office' objective.
tension: The ch.7 argument is tactical and conditional ('not yet politically obsolete'), and it conflicts with the project's insurgent/revolutionary path if the player abstains. The game should model the cost and benefit of participation and not hard-code Lenin's conclusion.

citations.quote: participation in parliamentary elections and in the struggle on the parliamentary rostrum is obligatory on the party of the revolutionary proletariat
for the purpose of educating the backward strata of its own class

claim: Stalin's definition: a nation is a historically constituted, stable community formed on common language, territory, economic life and psychological make-up manifested in a common culture, and it exists only when all the characteristics are present together.
game_relevance: Stalin's test is checkable against data fields (language, territory, economic life), which supports ADR171 naming Black, Chicano and Indigenous nations from observed attributes. For the class-agent design, nation is a second axis on each cohort that overlaps class (a cohort has both a class position and a national membership). The 'all together' rule argues against deriving a nation from a single census flag.
tension: ADR171 declares non-contiguous, people-attached nations with an overlap policy; Stalin's 'common territory' criterion is in tension with non-contiguous nations, and the MIM line departs from it. The ruling governs, so use the Stalin definition only as the analytical background, and do not reinfer authority from it.

citations.quote: A nation is a historically constituted, stable community of people, formed on the basis of a common language, territory, economic life, and psychological make-up manifested in a common culture.
It is only when all these characteristics are present together that we have a nation.

claim: The repo's own statement of the class principle already matches the sources: class position is about living, control of work and returns, and population groups get a part in play when they can decide. The ported rule packs (consciousness, solidarity, class-dynamics, imperial-rent) exist as BSL content, and the imperial-rent pack header says wages, subsidy and decision stages 'are not implemented here'.
game_relevance: The source-derived class and bribery logic has a partly ported home in the rule packs, but the wage/bribe stage that would implement Lenin's mechanism is explicitly unported in that pack. A class-agent design should reuse those packs' names and pools and not invent a parallel mechanism. Whether the national campaign loads them was not verified here.

citations.quote: Class position concerns how people make a living, who controls their work and who receives its returns.
Wages, subsidy and decision are not implemented here.

verification_note: NORTH_STAR lines 64-70: sentence is a line-wrapped 'Class position concerns how people make a living, who controls their work / and who receives its returns.' (found). The imperial-rent header line is 'Circuit. Wages, subsidy and decision are not implemented here.' (spans lines 5-6; locator corrected). Files consciousness.bsl, solidarity.bsl, class-dynamics.bsl, imperial-rent.bsl exist in the rules directory; the claim that they match the sources was not otherwise tested.

claim: The hypergraph store has an attributed-membership payload slot on every (member, hyperedge) incidence edge, described as 'Carried, empty, unhashed', and it is the structurally right home for Amendment AG(i) / ADR189 attributed membership.
game_relevance: Membership of a household cohort in an organization (the Hunan one-name-per-family model) has a ready slot. Writing to it will change the hashed state and may need an amendment or ruling first, since the slot is unhashed today.
tension: Using the slot is a design change the Director has not authorised for this program, and putting values in it alters the determinism surface.

citations.quote: Carried, empty, unhashed — nothing in this train writes it.

claim: Reading the sources together, a cohort's class position and its disposition are two separate derived quantities. Class position (Lenin, Mao 1933) comes from income sources and ownership. Disposition (Mao 1926, Hunan) comes from the material balance and trend plus the visible strength of competing organizations. The two should not be collapsed into one tag.
game_relevance: Same class, different choices: surplus, break-even and deficit cohorts of one class position (Mao's three petty-bourgeois sections) differ. This implements NORTH_STAR's 'residents can share a class position and choose different organizations or decline to join one' without inventing individual agents.

citations.quote: Although all strata of this class have the same petty-bourgeois economic status, they fall into three different sections.

claim: Proposal: derive each cohort's class stratum each period from existing accounts as a categorical read-out, using Mao 1933 dominant-source logic plus the Lenin bribe test. Inputs: share of income from wages sold, own-labour production, hired labour or profit, rent/interest/dividends, and transfers, plus the sign of wage versus value of labour power. Read out: worker, bribed worker (wage above value), own-account (middle), indebted semi-proletarian (poor, selling part of its labour), employer, rentier. Never store it as a tag that the player can edit.
game_relevance: This gives the 'who' without individual agents: the cohort count and the derived stratum define groups, and choices (look for work, move county, join/leave an organization, back a delegate, vote) read from the stratum and the balance trend. Each threshold must be recorded as Observed, Derived, Calibrated or Designed.
tension: The bribed-worker test needs a value-of-labour-power measure per cohort; whether the campaign has one is not verified, and the memory warns against unweighted means of intensive variables across classes or space.

citations.quote: the poor peasant has to sell part of his labour power.

claim: Proposal: organizations compete for cohort choices through a rank-order allocation, with no threshold or sigmoid. Each period every cohort ranks the organizations it can reach by the material fit of what they deliver to its accounts and by their demonstrated strength, and the active third joins first, the intermediate waits for visible power (Hunan second period), and the backward are won only through explanatory work. Organizer capacity is the budget.
game_relevance: This turns the mass line and the Hunan staging into a mechanism that stays inside the 'rank-order under a budget' rule. It also makes the player's real constraint organizer time and results, so the entertainment comes from sequencing which strata to organise first.
tension: The active/intermediate/backward split must be an emergent ordering of cohorts by risk and stake, not a fixed one-third partition.

citations.quote: The leaders must therefore be skilled in uniting the small number of active elements around the leadership

claim: Proposal: split consciousness into at least two derived channels. A trade-union channel (economist demands such as wages, work, relief) rises from the cohort's own account pressure. A political channel rises only through organization practice, and aid alone must not raise it.
game_relevance: Gives Lenin's spontaneity-versus-consciousness a gameplay consequence: relief hearings and wage fights win economist loyalty cheaply, but a revolutionary or electoral project needs sustained organizational work, so the player faces a real tradeoff and an opponent (the labour-aristocratic or reformist organization) can win the economist channel.
tension: PER-337 forbids inferring political consciousness from aid. Any link from material gain to the political channel must pass through an organization's recorded practice. A two-channel split may also count as a new formal element and needs a material relation for each channel before it is adopted.

citations.quote: the working class, exclusively by its own effort, is able to develop only trade union consciousness

not_found: Eighteenth Brumaire ch.7 in the local mirror (only ch01 and ch02 exist at /media/user/data/old-hdd/old-hdd/www.marxists.org/archive/marx/works/1852/18th-brumaire/); fetched from marxists.org instead
Poverty of Philosophy ch.2 s.5 in the local mirror (only ch01b, ch02b, ch02c exist)
Engels's 1892 preface to The Condition of the Working Class locally (1892/ directory absent) and at the standard URLs tried; reached only through marxists.org 1892/07/21 via fetch summary
Engels to Marx, 7 Oct 1858 in full (locally 58_10_08 exists but is a different letter); only the final clause was captured
Full text of Engels to Kautsky 12 Sep 1882 locally (no archive/engels directory)
Engels 1895 introduction in the local mirror (class-struggles-france has only ch02, ch03)
gaps: The Marx-Surplus.pdf file is a rough scan or excerpt of Theories of Surplus Value, and I read only the unproductive-labour passage. I did not read Capital I ch.25 section 2 (the progressive production of a relative surplus population) or section 5 (illustrations). I did not check Capital III chapters on wages and the labour market. The web-fetched quotes (M14, M16 to M22) came through a fetch-and-summarise tool, not raw page text. Of these, M14 and M16 are reliable and the others (M19 to M22) need re-verification against the full text. Printed page numbers for Capital I are from the running heads in the PDF text extraction, and the pdf page numbering is offset by one. I did not verify the engine claims about what the Rust engine does today, and did not check the Linear, ADR or hypergraph material. Neither the Gramsci, Althusser nor MIM material was in scope for this assignment.
verifier_notes: All 26 findings were kept. Local sources were checked by text extraction. Capital I and III quotes were found with the printed page numbers given. The Capital II quote was found on pdf p.33. The Manifesto quotes were found in the local mirror. The Poverty of Philosophy, Brumaire, 1858, 1882, 1892 and 1895 quotes were checked by WebFetch. That tool caps quote length at 125 characters, so M19 and M20 are confirmed only at clause level. Three findings were corrected. M13: the 'ideological class' sentence reports what apologists proclaimed, not Marx calling the dependence a fact. M21: the claim that the English working class will lose its privilege when the monopoly breaks was not confirmed and was dropped. M22: 'has become antiquated' was narrowed to what the returned text says. The Constitution and ADR171 context claims in M11, M25 and M26 were not independently verified. The Manifesto line numbers in M17 and M18 are approximate.

claim: Capital III ch.52 asks what constitutes a class and answers first that class position is the identity of revenues and sources of revenue: wage-labourers, capitalists and landowners live on wages, profit and ground-rent, i.e. on realising labour-power, capital, land.
game_relevance: Class position should be derived from a household's revenue sources (wages, ownership income, rent, transfers), not assigned as a label. This matches NORTH_STAR's definition and a household that mixes revenue types sits in several class positions at once.

citations.locator: Capital III ch.52 Classes, p.576 per the PDF table of contents (line 28390 of the extraction)
citations.quote: At first glance – the identity of revenues and sources of revenue.

claim: Marx himself shows revenue-source identity is insufficient: by that test physicians and officials would form two classes, and landlords, capitalists and labourers fragment endlessly by interest and rank. The manuscript breaks off there, so Marx gives no finished criterion.
game_relevance: Do not make class a fixed taxonomy of revenue-source buckets. Use revenue source as the material basis and let groups form from organization and struggle (M5, M7). Sub-groups such as occupations or stagnant-layer households are legitimate when they act differently.

citations.quote: physicians and officials, e.g., would also constitute two classes
[Here the manuscript breaks off.]

tension: NORTH_STAR says residents can share a class position and still choose differently. That is consistent. Class is not a complete predictor of choice.

claim: Capital III ch.52 also states that even in England classes do not appear in pure form because middle and intermediate strata blur the lines, and Marx sets this aside as immaterial to the analysis. The three-class scheme is a tendency of capitalist production, not a census.
game_relevance: Model the three pure positions as limits and let intermediate positions (petty owners, professionals, state employees, mixed-revenue households) appear as mixtures of revenue shares. This avoids forcing every cohort into one of three bins.

citations.quote: Middle and intermediate strata even here obliterate lines of demarcation everywhere

claim: Capital I ch.6: labour-power is sold by a worker who is free in a double sense, free to dispose of it as a commodity and with no other commodity to sell. This condition is historical, not natural.
game_relevance: The labor-market actor is a household with no means of production, selling hours. A household's control over means of production (land, a business, savings) determines whether it must sell labor-power. This is the 'who controls their work' line in NORTH_STAR and the basis for the stop-looking-for-work choice.

citations.quote: free in the double sense, that as a free man he can dispose of his labour-power as his own commodity

claim: Capital I ch.6: the value of labour-power includes a historical and moral element and the means of subsistence for the worker's substitutes (children), so that the race of labour-power owners can perpetuate itself on the market.
game_relevance: Labor supply is reproduced by households through births, aging and a subsistence bundle that varies by place and period. This supports the existing household lifecycle (births, ages 16-17, 18-64, 65+) as the real source of labor supply and argues for a county-varying, historically determined needs basket rather than one constant.

citations.quote: there enters into the determination of the value of labour-power a historical and moral element.
the means necessary for the labourer's substitutes, i.e., his children

claim: Capital I ch.25 s.3: the relative surplus population is a necessary product of accumulation and also a condition of its existence. It forms a disposable industrial reserve army that belongs to capital 'quite as absolutely as if the latter had bred it at its own cost'.
game_relevance: The unemployed/reserve pool is not a leftover. It is a structurally produced state that regulates wages. The existing 'employed + reserve = labor force' accounting should be read as this relation, so reserve counts should respond to accumulation and technical change (hires and separations).

citations.quote: It forms a disposable industrial reserve army, that belongs to capital quite as absolutely as if the latter had bred it at its own cost.

claim: Capital I ch.25 s.3: the reserve army weighs on the active army in stagnation and holds its pretensions in check in boom, and is 'the pivot upon which the law of demand and supply of labour works'. Marx adds that if workers try by trade unions to organise 'co-operation between employed and unemployed', capital and political economy cry out against it.
game_relevance: Wage pressure should be an emergent function of reserve-pool size relative to employment. A key organizing action for the player is linking employed and unemployed, which directly attacks the mechanism that disciplines wages. A claimants' assembly or workplace committee that joins the two is Marx's own case of workers becoming an actor.

citations.quote: Relative surplus population is therefore the pivot upon which the law of demand and supply of labour works.
organise a regular co-operation between employed and unemployed

tension: The project's no-imposed-response-curve rule means wage pressure cannot be a fixed curve of reserve share. It has to come out of the bargaining/hiring mechanics.

claim: Capital I ch.25 s.4 names three standing forms of the relative surplus population, all defined by relation to employment: floating (centres of industry, repelled and attracted, youths discharged at maturity), latent (rural population on the point of passing into the urban proletariat), stagnant (part of the active army with extremely irregular employment, maximum working time, minimum wages, domestic industry). A fourth sphere is pauperism.
game_relevance: These are candidate labor-supply states for household cohorts: floating = recently separated and searching; latent = non-participating rural or other-county households that migrate when openings appear; stagnant = precarious, underpaid, irregular-hours workers; pauper = unable to work or long-term dependent. They map to the 'keep looking or stop' and 'move county' choices and need explicit state counts with conserved transitions.

citations.quote: it has always three forms, the floating, the latent, the stagnant.
The third category of the relative surplus population, the stagnant, forms a part of the active labour army, but with extremely irregular employment.

claim: Capital I ch.25 s.4 on the latent form: the constant flow of rural population to towns presupposes 'a constant latent surplus population, the extent of which becomes evident only when its channels of outlet open to exceptional width'. The agricultural labourer stands with one foot in the swamp of pauperism.
game_relevance: Migration should be a bounded household choice driven by openings elsewhere. Rural counties hold hidden labor reserves that show up only when a destination county hires, so the labor force in a county is not observable from its current employment alone.

citations.quote: a constant latent surplus population, the extent of which becomes evident only when its channels of outlet open to exceptional width

claim: Capital I ch.25 s.4: stagnant-layer families are larger and reproduce faster, in inverse proportion to wages. Pauperism is 'the hospital of the active labour-army and the dead weight of the industrial reserve army' and consists of able-bodied paupers who rise and fall with the cycle, orphans and pauper children, and the demoralised and those unable to work.
game_relevance: Fertility and household size can legitimately differ by cohort income without individual agents, and a pauper layer composed of three conserved sub-states (able but cast out, child dependents, unable to work) rises with each crisis. This also gives relief and claimant organizing a material base. It is a Calibrated-class parameter, not a law to hard-code.

citations.quote: Pauperism is the hospital of the active labour-army and the dead weight of the industrial reserve army.
the quantity of paupers increases with every crisis, and diminishes with every revival of trade

tension: The inverse relation of family size to wages is a nineteenth-century empirical claim. Treat it as a Calibrated input checked against ACS and fertility data, not as doctrine.

claim: Capital I ch.25 s.4 states the absolute general law: the greater the social wealth and the reserve army relative to the active army, the greater the consolidated surplus population and official pauperism, and the lot of the labourer 'be his payment high or low, must grow worse'.
game_relevance: Marx separates the wage level from the worker's position. High pay does not remove the structural precarity. This supports tracking relative position (reserve pressure, security, dependence) alongside income, and not reading a good wage as an escape from class position.

citations.quote: in proportion as capital accumulates, the lot of the labourer, be his payment high or low, must grow worse.

tension: MIM's bribe thesis (ADR171, positive balance of wage over value) departs from the immiseration reading and treats part of the First World working population as a labor aristocracy. This is a theory-line choice to confirm with the Director rather than resolve by design.

claim: Capital II: labour-power is maintained and reproduced by the worker's individual consumption, which capital presupposes but which falls outside the circuit of the individual capital.
game_relevance: Household consumption (pantry, cash, needs) is the reproduction of labour-power and sits outside the firm circuit. This justifies households as the unit that holds the labor-supply stock and decides on it, with firms only buying the hours.

citations.locator: Ch.1 (M-C circuit of money capital), pdf p.33
citations.quote: the worker maintains and reproduces himself as labour-power by means of his individual consumption.

claim: Theories of Surplus Value (excerpt in Marx-Surplus.pdf): Marx notes that state officials, military, doctors, priests, judges and lawyers found it unpleasant to be classed with 'clowns and servants' as mere consumers, and that political economy came to see the necessity for these largely unproductive classes as arising from capitalist organisation itself. He describes them as faux frais of production for Smith and the capitalists. The apologists then proclaimed the dependence of the 'ideological etc. class' on the capitalists.
game_relevance: Salaried professional and state-employee cohorts (the middle strata) are a distinct group whose revenue comes from surplus value or taxes. They can be represented as such, with their own interests in the state and ideology, rather than being merged into the proletariat or bourgeoisie.

citations.locator: Theories of Surplus Value, printed pp.175-176 (pdf extraction lines 2064-2102)
citations.quote: The dependence of the ideological etc. class on the capitalists was in fact proclaimed.

verification_note: The quote is real, on printed p.176. The original claim said 'the text calls the dependence a fact', which misreads it. The sentence reports that the sycophants of bourgeois society proclaimed that dependence, in the context of restoring the prestige of 'parasitic' sections. The 'clowns and servants' and 'arose from its own organisation' material is on p.175. The claim is narrowed accordingly. The 'surplus value or taxes' revenue gloss and the 'distinct group' conclusion are design inference, not Marx's statement, and Marx treats these strata as faux frais.

claim: Poverty of Philosophy ch.2 s.5: capital makes the mass of workers a common mass with common interests, 'already a class as against capital, but not yet for itself'. In the struggle (combination) the mass unites and 'constitutes itself as a class for itself', and 'the struggle of class against class is a political struggle'.
game_relevance: Core translation for this design: class position (in itself) is derived from material accounts, but acting as a class (for itself) is a state that organization and struggle produce. A group moves from latent to organized class agent through joint practice (combination, strikes, assemblies), not by default. This supports giving groups choices only conditional on organizational reach and prior struggle.

citations.locator: Ch.2, s.5 'Strikes and Combinations of Workers'
citations.quote: This mass is thus already a class as against capital, but not yet for itself.
But the struggle of class against class is a political struggle.

tension: The local mirror holds ch02b/ch02c only, not this section, so it was fetched from marxists.org. The summarized text was verified for the quoted sentences only.

claim: Poverty of Philosophy: combination 'always has a double aim', stopping competition among workers so they can compete generally with the capitalist.
game_relevance: Organizing's first function is suppressing worker-against-worker competition (the reserve-army mechanism of M7). A workplace committee or claimants' assembly that sets a wage or hiring floor is the game's version, and the choice 'join an organization' is a bet on trading short-term individual advantage for collective bargaining.

citations.quote: Thus combination always has a double aim, that of stopping competition among the workers

claim: Eighteenth Brumaire ch.7: small-holding peasants 'form a class' by economic conditions but, lacking local interconnection and political organization, 'the identity of their interests forms no community, no national bond'. They are like potatoes in a sack and 'cannot represent themselves, they must be represented'.
game_relevance: A class can exist as a revenue-position count without being able to act. Dispersed groups (rural small owners, isolated reserve households, the stagnant layer) should have no collective choice unless some organization or delegate reaches them. This is a direct warrant for the 'back or withhold a delegate' choice and for representation to come from organizations.

citations.quote: much as potatoes in a sack form a sack of potatoes
They cannot represent themselves, they must be represented.

tension: The local mirror lacks Brumaire ch.7 (only ch.1-2), so this was fetched from marxists.org. Brumaire also says the peasants are represented by someone who appears as their master. That cuts against the NORTH_STAR line that organizations compete for choices rather than rule over groups.

claim: Communist Manifesto ch.1: the proletariat is organised into a class and 'consequently into a political party', and this organisation is continually upset by competition among workers but 'ever rises up again, stronger'. Union is aided by communications and centralises local struggles into a national class struggle; 'every class struggle is a political struggle'.
game_relevance: Class organization is a recurring, contested outcome that decays under reserve-army competition (M7) and rebuilds through practice. Model class organization as a stock that can fall and be rebuilt, helped by connectivity (hypergraph and county adjacency), not as a threshold event.

citations.locator: Ch.1 Bourgeois and Proletarians, lines ~391-399 of tag-stripped text
citations.quote: This organisation of the proletarians into a class, and, consequently into a political party, is continually being upset again by the competition between the workers themselves.

claim: Communist Manifesto ch.1: lower middle class (small manufacturer, shopkeeper, artisan, peasant) fight the bourgeoisie to save their existence, so are 'conservative' and 'reactionary', and are revolutionary only in view of impending transfer into the proletariat. The lumpenproletariat is more prepared 'for the part of a bribed tool of reactionary intrigue'.
game_relevance: The petty-owner group and the lumpen/precarious group have predictable political directions, with the former defending a threatened position and the latter open to being bought. This gives the electoral and organization contest asymmetric recruits and a reason for reactionary organizations to compete for them.

citations.quote: They are therefore not revolutionary, but conservative.
far more for the part of a bribed tool of reactionary intrigue

tension: The Manifesto's lumpenproletariat label is moralised and differs from Capital I's pauper layer (M10). Do not assign political direction by a layer's label. Let it follow from relation to organizations and the balance sign.

claim: Engels to Marx, 7 Oct 1858: the English proletariat is becoming more bourgeois, so that the nation aims at 'a bourgeois aristocracy and a bourgeois proletariat' alongside the bourgeoisie. The fetched summary reproduced only the final clause of the sentence.
game_relevance: First Marx-Engels statement that a part of the working class can have interests tied to the dominant class's profits. This is the source line for the design of a wage-above-value group as a distinct, structurally bribed layer with its own choices.

citations.quote: alongside the bourgeoisie, of a bourgeois aristocracy and a bourgeois proletariat.

tension: Only the final clause was captured verbatim. Re-read the full sentence before citing in a design doc. The local mirror's 58_10_08 is a different letter (Marx to Engels).

claim: Engels to Kautsky, 12 Sep 1882: the English workers share the feast of England's monopoly of the world market and the colonies.
game_relevance: Material basis of the labor aristocracy: the source of the privilege is imperial position, not individual character. In Babylon the same logic ties cohort-level wage premium to the imperial-rent and trade systems (P26 TransportSystem, imperial-rent rules), which is what the project's balance sign encodes.

citations.quote: the workers gaily share the feast of England's monopoly of the world market and the colonies.

tension: The quote was returned through a summariser. Confirm exact wording and the surrounding sentences before using in a doc.

claim: Engels's 1892 preface to The Condition of the Working Class (marxists.org page 1892/07/21, the German-edition preface that reprints his 1885 article and his Jan 1892 English preface): the old unions 'form an aristocracy among the working class'. The East End is described as the home of 'New Unionism', the organisation of the great mass of 'unskilled' workers.
game_relevance: There are two organizing paths for the same class: craft-style unions of the privileged layer and mass organization of the unskilled. Both are plausible organizations for groups to join, with different reach and different interest in preserving the privilege.

citations.quote: They form an aristocracy among the working class;

citations.locator: 1892 preface, quoting the Jan 1892 English preface (East End passage)
citations.quote: of the organisation of the great mass of 'unskilled' workers

tension: The local mirror holds the Condition work (ch05, ch06 only) and not the preface. The quotes came from a fetch-and-summarise tool and are not verified against the full text.
verification_note: The page is the 1892 German-edition preface (21 July 1892) and both quotes are confirmed. The East End 'New Unionism' passage comes from the Jan 1892 English preface quoted in it, and the 'aristocracy' line from the 1885 article. The original claim also said the English working class 'will lose its privileged position once the manufacturing monopoly breaks'. That was not confirmed in this fetch, so it is dropped from the claim. The trailing semicolon in the first quote is in the source.

claim: Engels's 1895 introduction to The Class Struggles in France: German workers changed the franchise 'from a means of duping into an instrument of emancipation', which allows counting 'our numbers once every three years'. He writes that 'The rebellion of the old style, the street fight behind barricades' had given the final decision up to 1848, and that the bourgeoisie and government feared the legal action of the workers' party far more than the illegal action.
game_relevance: Elections as a class-organization measure. A vote is both a count of organized strength and an instrument whose value to a class depends on whether an organization contests it. This is Engels's case for an electoral project, which the MIM line disputes. The game should let electoral, reformist and revolutionary paths all be viable and emergent, per NORTH_STAR.

citations.quote: bourgeoisie and Government feared far more the legal than the illegal action of the workers’ party
The rebellion of the old style, the street fight behind barricades, which up to 1848 gave the final decision

tension: The quotes came through a summariser and the franchise quotes are fragments. The text is also contested (Engels objected to the editing of the 1895 text). The MIM literature is expected to reject the parliamentary road, which affects how electoral choices are framed.
verification_note: Confirmed by re-fetch: 'have changed it from a means of duping into an instrument of emancipation', 'to permit us to count our numbers once every three years', and the two cited quotes. The original claim said barricade fighting 'has become antiquated'. The returned text says only that such rebellion gave the final decision up to 1848, so the claim is narrowed to that. The editing-controversy and MIM remarks are context not checked here.

claim: The NORTH_STAR rules about class and groups line up with the Marx/Engels sources: class position is how people make a living, who controls their work and who receives returns; groups get a distinct part in play 'when they can make a decision of their own'; residents can share a class position and choose different organizations or decline to join.
game_relevance: Marx's own criterion (M14, M16) is the same: a class acts only when organized. The design can cite NORTH_STAR for the rule that membership is a choice, and Marx for the reason that a share of a class will always be unorganized.

citations.quote: Residents can share a class position and choose different organizations or decline to join one.

claim: NORTH_STAR also binds the design: households are the smallest economic decision unit and the economy does not simulate individual agents. This limits what a class-group choice can be.
game_relevance: Any 'group chooses X' must be a conserved-count transition on a household cohort (e.g. a share of searching workers stops looking), never a per-person agent. Reserve-army states must be count fields on cohorts.

citations.quote: The economy does not simulate individual agents.

claim: Proposal: derive class position from cohort accounts as revenue shares (wage, ownership, rent, transfer), classify the reserve states of M8 as explicit conserved counts with named transitions, and give each group a small choice set whose options depend on its organizational reach. Reserve pressure is the endogenous wage driver. No separate wage-curve is imposed.
game_relevance: Concrete shape of option 2 grounded in Marx: groups = (cohort revenue profile) x (labor-supply state) x (organizational ties). Choices per four-week period: keep searching or withdraw (floating to inactive), move county (latent to floating), join/leave organization, back or withhold a delegate, vote. Whether a group can act collectively depends on an organization reaching it (M16).

citations.quote: it has always three forms, the floating, the latent, the stagnant.

tension: Constitution: classify every substantive value as Observed/Derived/Calibrated/Designed and avoid new fixed response curves. Transition rates between reserve states must be Calibrated or emergent, and a new primitive needs Director approval.

claim: Interpretation: the sources disagree on what the working class does with a privileged layer. Capital I says conditions worsen for all workers, while Engels in 1858, 1882 and 1892 says a section shares in imperial monopoly and is organized in a way that preserves its position. The repo's bribe/deprivation finding (ADR171, 1.55 ratio) follows the Engels strand.
game_relevance: The design needs at least two working-class group types with opposed interests on the same issues (privileged/bribed versus deprived/stagnant). A single 'worker' group would hide the main political cleavage of the MIM line and the reason positive balance feeds the fascism-versus-revolution bifurcation.

citations.quote: be his payment high or low, must grow worse.
the workers gaily share the feast of England's monopoly of the world market and the colonies.

tension: This is the central tension for the theory line. Resolve it with the MIM sources, not by choosing between Marx and Engels here. Any change to the reserved theory line requires asking the Director.
