claim: MCU says it concentrates its organizing on the advanced workers in the labor unions, especially the industrial proletariat. It plans to reach the intermediate and backward workers through them. It is explicitly a pre-party organization (a vanguard party is its goal), not a party.
game_relevance: A rival organization with a recruitment target defined by position in a workplace and union (industrial, unionized, advanced) rather than by nation or prison status. In play it competes for union-militant cohorts of employed workers, who are a small, workplace-bound share of the population. MIM's line reads those same cohorts as mostly labor aristocracy, so their material reasons for joining must come from the accounts.

citations.quote: We concentrate our organizing efforts and propaganda on the advanced workers in the labor union movement, especially the industrial proletariat.
our primary task at present is to grow and develop as a pre-party organization

tension: NORTH_STAR says class concerns how people make a living and who controls their work. MCU's targeting by workplace and union position matches that, but under MIM's line the same cohorts are mostly oppressor-nation wage earners.
source_standing: OPPOSED LINE (MCU): by Director ruling, settler communist and opposed to the MIM line. Evidence of what that line says or does; never support for the game's own method.

claim: MCU's own self-criticism says it cannot currently make leading proletarian struggle its main focus. Its main work is growing the organization and winning over 'semi-Marxists': college-educated, petty-bourgeois youth entering working-class jobs and unions. It uses studies, a contact system with a supporter tier, online agitation aimed at activists, and national mass organizations under its leadership.
game_relevance: First recruits to this rival are activist and student cohorts, not the industrial workers it names as its target. In play it should be small, study-and-contact based, and spend most capacity on internal growth, not strike leadership.

citations.quote: educated and petty-bourgeois background, is pouring into working-class jobs and
the bulk of our agitation and propaganda must be directed towards activists

verification_note: Quotes found; the first is line-wrapped, so I trimmed it to the text actually on the page (the original began 'largely from a college-educated', which is split across lines and not contiguous in the pdf text). The 'cannot, at present, make leading the struggles of the proletariat our main focus' (line 27) is the actual source for the 'cannot lead' claim; I narrowed 'cannot currently lead working-class struggle' to 'cannot make leading proletarian struggle its main focus'. Contact/supporter/cadre and national mass organization confirmed.
source_standing: OPPOSED LINE (MCU): by Director ruling, settler communist and opposed to the MIM line. Evidence of what that line says or does; never support for the game's own method.

claim: MCU holds the labor aristocracy is 'only a small subsection of the working class', not equivalent to union membership. It is the base of reactionary union leaders. Its privileges have eroded since the mid-1970s. MCU says it does not yet know how large it is, and calls for more investigation.
game_relevance: This is the opposed line's answer to the question the game must settle: MCU treats most union members as proletarian, so it offers them an anti-business-union program. Babylon should not treat the aristocracy's size as a free parameter. The engine measures it from accounts, and the rival's claim is a hypothesis that can be tested against those accounts.

citations.quote: the labor aristocracy which is only a small subsection of the working class
how large it ever truly got and how large it is today

tension: Conflicts with the Director's ruling and the ADR171 bribe-mass calculation, which put the bribed population far above 'small'.
source_standing: OPPOSED LINE (MCU): by Director ruling, settler communist and opposed to the MIM line. Evidence of what that line says or does; never support for the game's own method.

claim: MIM's contrary position: imperialist-country working classes are primarily a bought-off labor aristocracy, a new petty-bourgeoisie, and not the principal vehicle for Maoism there. MIM's program says they would be 'on the receiving end' of the dictatorship of the international proletariat.
game_relevance: This is the game's own line (Director ruling). It sets the default reading of a US wage-earning cohort: the bribe, not the wage, determines how the cohort responds. A rival whose strategy depends on those cohorts being proletarian is predicted to be pulled toward economism and reformism, and the accounts decide whether that happens.

citations.quote: These so-called workers bought off by imperialism form a new petty-bourgeoisie called the labor aristocracy.
we believe that the imperialist-country working classes are primarily a pro-imperialist labor aristocracy at this time

claim: MCU's union strategy follows the CPUSA's 1920s TUEL model: build a 'militant minority' left opposition by boring from within existing reactionary unions, lead organizing drives of the unorganized, later independent unions as united fronts. It targets sellout contracts and reactionary leaders (the UPS 'Vote No' campaign is its example) and takes abolition of the wages system as the watchword.
game_relevance: Its offers are inside the union: contested elections, no-votes on contracts, organizing drives. It competes with business-union leadership and social-democratic caucuses; costs are staff time and retaliation. No lever outside unionized workplaces.

citations.quote: boring-from-within and building this MMO/left opposition in and across the unions
nationally in the “Vote No” campaign
make abolition of the wages system the watchword of the trade union movement

The UPS contract struggle is at line 195. 'Revolutionary trade union center' (third stage) not individually re-read; independent-unions-as-united-fronts confirmed at lines 262-270.

claim: MIM's FAQ says union struggles in the US, with the exception of immigrant, migrant and prisoner unions, only lead to a further crackdown on 'other WHITE workers exploited in the ex-Soviet bloc and Central Asia'. It tells imperialist-country whites to organize on behalf of those 300 million exploited white workers in eastern Europe, Russia and Central Asia.
game_relevance: Under MIM's line a wage victory by a unionized first-world cohort is a transfer that does not weaken imperialism and may raise that cohort's bribe margin. Babylon should record the transfer in accounts and keep the label out of it. Which unions count (immigrant, migrant, prisoner) matters more than density.

citations.quote: Fighting union struggles in the united $tates --with the exception of immigrant, migrant and prisoner unions-- only leads to a further crackdown on other WHITE workers exploited in the ex-Soviet bloc and Central Asia.

tension: The FAQ is a 2001 text with provocative wording, and its claim about 'crackdown on other WHITE workers' is not verified for the game. It is MIM's stated line. NORTH_STAR requires no label to predetermine success, so the engine measures it and does not script the prediction.

The original claim said MIM tells people to link with the 'exploited Third World and prison proletariat'; the source instead names exploited white workers in the ex-Soviet bloc/Central Asia as the object, and says 'crackdown on' them, not a squeeze on workers abroad generally. Narrowed accordingly. The date '2001' was not verified.

claim: MCU wants unions to take up political action independent of the bourgeois parties and, as a united front, to form a mass electoral Labor Party with communists keeping independence, while saying the timing is unsettled. Its W2W statement critically endorses a left caucus resolution in NYC-DSA while saying the premise that the mayor is a movement leader who can be pushed left is flawed because he is 'an enemy of the people and member of the ruling class', and calls proposing to respect a tenant vote on privatization 'a fetishization of the electoral form'. Its flyer calls Sanders-style politics 'Bernie's tepid social democracy' and groups it with Trump and Biden populisms.
game_relevance: This rival does not run candidates itself. It works inside vehicles run by others, pressures office-holders, and uses betrayal for propaganda. In the electoral system it holds delegates and pressure inside a party it does not control.

citations.quote: forming a mass electoral Labor Party as a special kind of united front
rather than being an enemy of the people and member of the ruling class
a fetishization of the electoral form
Bernie’s tepid social democracy

verification_note: All quotes found. Corrections: (1) the 'enemy of the people' line is MCU rejecting a premise 'rather than being an enemy...', i.e. it asserts the mayor IS one; claim reworded to say so. (2) 'Bernie's tepid social democracy' is in the MCU flyer, not the W2W statement; added as a flyer citation. (3) 'fetishization' applies to the argument that a tenant majority vote legitimizes privatization, not to electoral work generally. (4) The 2026 date is not printed in the statement text; it refers to DSA's 2025 convention as past, so 2026 is inferred. The 'timing unsettled' claim matches lines 210-214.
source_standing: OPPOSED LINE (MCU): by Director ruling, settler communist and opposed to the MIM line. This finding also cites other sources; only the part resting on the tagged text is opposed-line evidence. Evidence of what that line says or does; never support for the game's own method.

claim: MIM's contrary position: do not vote, organize. An elected individual makes no difference under an imperialist state. Only candidates with wealthy backing can run. Elections mostly split the benefits of imperialism between sections of the middle class. MIM's program also holds that armed struggle in the imperialist countries is premature until the bourgeoisie is helpless.
game_relevance: This fixes what an election can and cannot change in the game: it can move allocations among the bribed. It does not change who holds state power or the imperialist surplus. MCU's labor party and critical-endorsement tactics are predicted to deliver office-holders who serve the same state. The engine should still let elections shift real allocations (budgets, grants), because the player may pursue an electoral project and outcomes come from accounts.

citations.quote: don't vote, organize!
these differences are very minor and generally come down to tactical tweaks in domestic policy issues

tension: NORTH_STAR requires a working electoral system before endorsements and says direction emerges from practice. MIM says electoral work is largely futile, so the design needs the system to exist without scripting its irrelevance.

claim: MCU's model: three stages for union work (pre-party, party plus militant-minority organization, revolutionary union center). It builds in a deliberate order (grow MCU, then the left opposition, then a party). It concentrates forces: it criticizes its earlier line of 'going everywhere and doing everything'. It holds that a mass organization of the advanced helps a party reach a broad section of the labor movement. It uses a contact system (contact, supporter, cadre) with democratic centralism.
game_relevance: A rival organization needs a finite cadre budget with a focus choice, because MCU itself says it cannot be everywhere. It has a recruitment funnel (contact, supporter, cadre) and internal costs (study time, discipline). These fit the project rule that organizations compete for bounded choices and have capacity limits. They are not a script for how the player must organize.

citations.quote: concentrating the bulk of our efforts on growing MCU
get this contact involved in a national study, and then have them join a national mass organization

claim: FRSO's program says the working class is the majority and will be the 'main and leading force' for change, and its strategy is a united front against the monopoly capitalist class that also draws in the petty bourgeoisie. It sees the urban poor as the stratum most open to revolutionary ideas and some upper sections as influenced by white and national chauvinism. It organizes a multinational working class including the poor and oppressed nationalities, plus a cross-class alliance through campaigns (labor, immigrants, antiwar). In play it can attract many group types, including petty-bourgeois cohorts, with a mass program. The cost is the contradiction between a wide alliance and any firm class line.

claim: MIM's lumpen and prisoner line. claim: On elections: MIM's slogan is 'Don't Vote, Organize.' claim: Proposed class derivation for household cohorts from existing accounts, using MIM's tests: (1) capital access (company shares, credit access, hired labor) separates bourgeoisie and petty bourgeoisie; (2) wage compared with a disclosed reproduction/value floor, for cohorts without capital access, separates labor aristocracy (above) from proletariat/semi-proletariat (at or below); (3) a cohort that is out of the labor force and not looking is excluded (lumpen), a separate state from the employed or reserve pool. National attribute stays declared (ADR171) and is a separate axis. Choices are bounded and rank-ordered, such as keep looking or stop, move county, join, attend or leave an organization, back or withhold a delegate, and vote. Organizations compete for those choices under a budget, with no new primitive and no sigmoid.
game_relevance: Gives a path that keeps cohorts as conserved counts, classes as derived views, and organizations as the actors competing for choices. It also puts the contested above-value test in plain view of the Director.
tension: Needs a ruling on the reproduction floor, on whether the external transfer is Designed or Calibrated, and on whether class labels are shown to players. A US-only simulation cannot confirm MIM's thesis. It can only apply it with a declared transfer channel. If the floor is computed in-country, some low-wage cohorts will read as proletariat and conflict with the 'no US proletariat' line. That is the point the Director must decide, per AGENTS.md. Do not decide it in code.

claim: MIM sorts workers into four cells by two tests: productive vs unproductive sector, and exploited vs not. In imperialist countries cell (a) exploited productive workers is, on MIM's account, effectively empty (MIM disputes Cockshott's claim of an exploited minority in England, saying transfer leaves these workers no net surplus labor-time) and cell (b) exploited unproductive workers does not exist there. Cells (c) unexploited productive and (d) unexploited unproductive hold the majority. MIM maps the labor aristocracy roughly onto (c)+(d), 'semi-proletarian ... hardened into a peacetime petty-bourgeoisie'. Cell (b) is the only one whose class is left open.
game_relevance: A household-cohort classifier can use this 2x2: a sector tag on the employing workplace crossed with a net-transfer test (does the wage exceed what the cohort's own labor creates once inflows are counted). The default for US cohorts is (c) or (d), not 'proletarian'.

There is also no reason the number cannot exceed 100 percent of unproductive sector income.

tension: The multiplier 8 (or 10) is a fixed calibration constant. Under the Constitution it must be classed Calibrated with its basis, and must not act as a second fixed response curve. MIM's own text calls it counterfactual; treat any result as unchecked.

claim: Wage facts MIM uses on the Third World side: average Third World wage 48 cents per hour, export sector $1.24, China 50 cents in 1994 against $16.40 in the US (about 33 times). MIM recommends a monetization multiplier of 10 for Third World output. MIM's hours basis is 2,000 per year.
game_relevance: Calibration inputs if the engine reproduces MIM's superprofit term. The project convention is 2,080 hours per year, a 4 percent difference to note when reusing MIM's worker-count conversions.

citations.quote: MIM recommends using a multiplier parameter of 10 whenever some production in the Third World comes up in discussion.
The Financial Times in 1994 reported that average manufacturing wages in China per hour were 50 cents, which meant U.$. wages of $16.40 an hour were nearly 33 times higher.
At 2000 hours a year for 50 cents an hour, that is the work of 80 million workers.

claim: There is no numeric wage at which a US worker stops being exploited. MIM's nearest statements are about the legal minimum wage and the world income ranking: a US minimum-wage earner at 2,000 hours is in the top 10 percent of most countries; a US minimum wage of $5.15 is 2.5 times the best-paid skilled worker at a Fiji plant. The test is net transfer, not a threshold.
game_relevance: Do not hard-code a wage cutoff. Use the sign of (wage received minus value the cohort's own productive labor creates), with the legal wage floor only as the marker of who sits outside it. MIM gives no cutoff to calibrate.

citations.quote: if we take a minimum wage earner in the united $tates working 2000 hours a year, that persyn would be in the top 10% of most countries in the world.
The lowest possible pay goes to U.$. minimum wage workers who will earn $5.15 an hour, which is still 2.5 times more than that of any skilled worker at Nestle's in Fiji.

tension: Constitution: no imposed sigmoid or fixed response curve; a sign test avoids adding a threshold constant.

claim: Productive/unproductive rule MIM takes from Shaikh and Tonak: distribution (excluding some transport), social maintenance and reproduction, and personal consumption are unproductive; Marx counted all government activity as unproductive; even inside US manufacturing 34.9 percent of employees (1994) are not production workers. MIM adds that guards, soldiers, salespeople and lawyers can only preserve or appropriate surplus-value, not expand it.
game_relevance: A workplace sector tag is not enough: staffing pools need an occupation split (production vs non-production) so a manufacturing workplace contributes both productive and unproductive hours. County government payroll, health and education are unproductive in this frame.

citations.quote: in the sectors of distribution (excluding some transportation), social maintenance and reproduction and personal consumption, any labor that occurs is not productive sector labor.
Karl Marx regarded all government activities as unproductive labor
34.9 percent of workers in manufacturing were not production workers

claim: Cell (b) workers (exploited but unproductive) can be either labor aristocracy or proletarian 'depending on the balance of other workers in the country who are exerting a pull'. Class position is partly contextual: the surrounding mix of workers pulls a group one way or the other.
game_relevance: A cohort's class reading could depend on its county or hypergraph neighbourhood (share of productive and unproductive workers) as well as its own account. This is the one place MIM supports a relational class rule.

citations.quote: MIM would contend that case b of workers could be either labor aristocracy or proletarian, depending in particular on the balance of other workers in the country who are exerting a pull on this group.

tension: Community is never a graph node (hex/community ruling): the 'balance of other workers' must be an aggregate over county or hypergraph incidence, not a community entity.

claim: Nation is not class. MIM says everyone inside imperialist borders, oppressed nation or not, may be an exploiter; the vast majority of employed Black, First Nation and Asian-descended people are labor aristocracy or higher, the exceptions being the undocumented and lumpen. Latino workers are the most proletarian (at least 42 percent in the productive sector in 1995), so a 'split in the working class' exists inside that nation. Classes and nations are 'groups of people not individuals or families'.
game_relevance: Nation must be a first-class dimension of every group but does not set class. A Black or Chicano wage-earning cohort defaults to labor aristocracy; the nation tag sets discrimination profit, group incidence and which organizations compete for the group.

citations.quote: Everyone within imperialist country borders whether nationally oppressed or not, may be exploiter, not exploited if the transfer of surplus-value from the Third World is large enough.
The vast majority of the employed Black, First Nation and Asian-descended peoples is labor aristocracy or higher.
Meanwhile, at least 42 percent of the Latino workers as of 1995 are in the productive sector.
Classes and nations are groups of people not individuals or families.

tension: ADR171 declares incidence 'people-attached' and never derived from c/v/s; MIM's class test is derived from c/v/s and wage floors. These are two separate axes and must not be merged into one score.

claim: Internal oppressed-nation labor supplies a large share of US surplus-value: Black and Latino workers were 12 percent each of 31.6 million productive-sector workers in 1995, farm workers were 40.3 percent Latino, and with 85 percent pay discrimination MIM concludes over 30 percent of surplus-value originating inside US borders comes from internal semi-colonies. The 1998 paper adds that Blacks as a nation rank above some advanced European countries in income (a claim carried from MT1, which was not readable here).
game_relevance: Numbers for seeding discrimination profit and for identifying which cohorts are the surplus-producing side of the productive sector; also shows a higher-income Black cohort is expected under this line, not an error.

citations.quote: Out of 31,592,000 productive sector workers, Blacks were 12 percent and Latinos another 12 percent.
it seems safe to say that over 30 percent of surplus-value that originates within U.S. borders is from internal semi-colonies of U.$. imperialism.
Blacks taken as a nation are ahead of some advanced European capitalist countries in terms of income.

tension: The income claim cites MT1; MT1 was not available locally, so it is unchecked.

claim: How a labor aristocracy hardens: Lenin's wording moved from bribed leaders, to a trend, to a stratum that leaves the working class, to a class. MIM frames it as 'first as a stratum and then as a class', and says the imperialists choose to share superprofit in wages rather than accumulate it. It also says oppressed-nation labor aristocracies are 'newer and less stable' than oppressor-nation ones.
game_relevance: Class position is a stock that hardens with time under positive net transfer, not a switch. A cohort flag for newly bought-off vs entrenched fits this; entrenched cohorts should be harder to move than new ones.

citations.quote: Thus, for Lenin, there is some issue as to how hardened the labor-aristocracy is--first as a stratum and then as a class.
what used to go to accumulation starts to show up in the wages of imperialist country workers and exaggerated military spending
True, such a labor-aristocracy will be newer and less stable than the labor aristocracy of the oppressor nations, but it is labor aristocracy nonetheless.

claim: What can re-proletarianize a labor aristocracy: MIM says only economic ruin and war on home soil (Lenin's conditions), or cutting off the Third World superprofit flow. It calls it highly likely that the labor aristocracy 'will never be re-proletarianized before communism', and cites Germany after 1945, where 're-proletarianization was little in evidence' despite devastation, and France 1968 as test cases.
game_relevance: Falling income alone does not turn a petty-bourgeois cohort into a proletarian one in MIM's account. Reversal needs the transfer term itself to shrink and the status basis to be lost; a 'ruin' event should reduce the superprofit term first and leave class labels sticky.

citations.locator: B.2 para 2 (item 2 of the list of five context points)
citations.quote: When Lenin was speaking of a working class in conditions of economic ruin and war, which were the only conditions which a parasite class could become re-proletarianized

citations.locator: C.7 paragraph on consolidation of the labor aristocracy
citations.quote: There is a high likelihood that the labor aristocracy will never be re-proletarianized before communism is achieved.
So in the event of getting super-profits cut off, you are right that proletarian struggle becomes possible in the imperialist countries.
despite the devastation of the war and the dire economic conditions, "re-proletarianization" was little in evidence.

tension: imp97 B.2 also says Lenin held that 'the crisis of the economy and imperialist war threatened to drive these petty-bourgeoisie back into the proletariat'. MIM's 'never' sits against that; MIM's resolution is that crisis opens the possibility but war on home soil is what it took.

claim: MIM's 'fear of loss' account of the petty-bourgeoisie: Lenin's 1921 line that petty-bourgeois democrats keep their hold on industrial and commercial workers and office employees 'who are afraid that if revolution breaks out they will lose the relative petty-bourgeois prosperity created by the privileges of imperialism'. MIM adds Lenin's point that the labor aristocracy fights hardest 'because of a psychology of being just above water'.
game_relevance: MIM's mechanism for group choice is defense of an existing superprofit share, not absolute deprivation. A cohort with a positive transfer balance should react to threats to that balance (jobs moving, imports cut, borders opening) before it reacts to its own income level.

citations.quote: who are afraid that if revolution breaks out they will lose the relative petty-bourgeois prosperity created by the privileges of imperialism
It was Lenin who taught that the labor aristocracy fights for imperialism more desperately than any other class, because of a psychology of being just above water and gasping for breath.

claim: MIM on fascism and the labor aristocracy: protectionism, anti-immigration and economic nationalism are the aristocracy's politics, and the same tactics 'unleash fascism' under a different class structure. MIM names the labor aristocracies and uncompetitive national capital as the major forces pushing toward separate national spheres and inter-imperialist war, and says an anti-foreign movement 'could easily take a national socialist direction in the United $tates'. Germany is the cited case: the aristocracy chose a strategy that 'depended on long-run military victory', with a negative profit rate in 1931-34. In Italy, where retail and banking dominate, neo-fascists won elections in the 1990s.
game_relevance: Supports the project finding that a positive balance (wage above value) redirects politics into chauvinist forms rather than suppressing it. MIM's trigger inputs are a threat to the transfer, a crisis in realizing it, and a nationalist organization to join; group size and sector matter more than income decline.

citations.quote: In another situation with a different class structure, the same strategy and tactics unleash fascism.

The major political forces pushing toward a return to separate spheres of national influence for each imperialism are the labor aristocracies of each country and the bourgeoisie of each country unable to compete on an international plane.
a movement for nationalization of Japanese assets, managed trade and against foreign influences could easily take a national socialist direction in the United $tates.
the labor aristocracy rejected the communist way out and willingly took up a strategy that depended on long-run military victory to be economically sustainable.
where neo-fascist candidates have won Italian elections in the 1990s.

tension: Heat design: escalation is rank-order under a budget with no threshold constant. MIM's account gives ordering inputs (transfer at risk, a nationalist organization available) and no constants; do not turn the loss-of-share logic into a threshold.

claim: MIM does not name 'falling status' as the cause of fascism. It says living standards in imperialist countries 'are not generally deteriorating' (a 1997 statement about the present, made in the context of Europe), argues that US labor-aristocracy wage complaints are overstated (MIM Notes 201: a 3.6 percent drop in annual earnings of 25-29 year-old white men, compared against 1978), and says what holds fascism back is division among the exploiters internationally, not an internal proletariat or liberals.
game_relevance: A pure falling-income trigger for fascism would contradict MIM's text. Build the reaction on defended share and external division among great powers, with relative loss as a second-order input.

citations.quote: Living standards are not generally deteriorating in the imperialist countries
This is hardly the catastrophe the labor aristocracy advocates describe.
Briefly put, what is preventing fascism is the nature of international division of the exploiters today.

tension: Consistent with the project memory finding (balance sign drives fascism-vs-revolution) but narrows it: objective income decline is not MIM's mechanism.
verification_note: Quotes found. Narrowed: the source gives 3.6 percent with a 1978 comparison year, not an explicit '20 years'; the 'not deteriorating' sentence is in a passage about Europe and definitions of the working class, not a direct fascism-cause argument. 'Does not name falling status as cause' is an absence claim, consistent with what was read but not exhaustively tested.

claim: Public-sector jobs and taxes are labor-aristocracy anchors in MIM's account: the government sector is 'the ultimate expression of the imperialists' loyalty to the oppressor nation working class' because it cannot be shipped overseas; rising taxation is 'a barometer of parasitism', not exploitation, when the money returns as government employment; military spending is backed by the aristocracy because it buys jobs.
game_relevance: County public budgets and payroll are class-forming in this frame. Raising county taxes that fund local jobs does not read as exploitation under MIM; cutting payroll or closing facilities hits the aristocratic anchor.

citations.quote: In some ways, the government sector is the ultimate expression of the imperialists' loyalty to the oppressor nation working class, since it is difficult to ship government service jobs overseas.
The increased taxation of German workers is actually a barometer of parasitism.

claim: Typical labor-aristocracy organizations and demands in MIM's account: AFL-CIO and other large unions (strikes at a 52-year low in 1999, and marches 'in defense of their privileged jobs'); a Teamsters item calling those workers labor aristocracy; prison guards as labor aristocrats whom the prison system employs; anti-immigrant ballot measures (Prop 187, including Black and Asian voters); the labor aristocracy outdoing the imperialists in viciousness against migrants. Protectionism is the standard demand.
game_relevance: Candidate group types for a county: craft and industrial union locals, public-employee and guard unions, homeowner and retiree blocs, nativist groups. Their decisions are about defending jobs and share, so 'joins a union' is not evidence of proletarian position.

citations.quote: In 1999, only 73,000 employees participated in strikes that involved 1,000 employees or more.
rather they were marching in defense of "their" privileged jobs.
MIM calls these workers labor aristocracy because they are receiving more than the value of their labor at the expense of exploited and superexploited workers in the Third World.
provides jobs to the labor aristocrats who guard them even as it indoctrinates them with fascist ideology
It was a disappointment to see voting Blacks and Asian-descended people go for Proposition 187 in California.
The labor aristocracy has made a big point in outdoing the imperialists in viciousness against the proletarian migrants.

tension: NORTH_STAR says residents can share a class position and choose different organizations. MIM's account makes the aristocracy's choices heavily predictable by position; keep it a pressure ordering, not a rule, to preserve choice.
verification_note: All six quotes found (52-year figure confirmed in MN225). Removed unsupported specifics from the original claim: 'UAW flyers', 'prison-guard union as aggressive', Social Security/Medicaid fights as part of this list (that is MC-25), and 'Minuteman-type groups' as a labor-aristocracy organization (the source says Trotskyists seek to unite with the Minuteman Project, and that MIM calls this reactionary; it does not classify the Minutemen as labor aristocracy). Teamsters item taken from mn106 only for the quoted sentence.

claim: Unions are classed by membership and purpose, not label: MIM treats big US unions as labor-aristocracy organizations but exempts 'immigrant, migrant and prisoner unions'. Lenin's Comintern resolution calls for replacing old labor-aristocratic leaders with workers tied to the exploited masses 'in proletarian organisations of absolutely every type'. MIM works inside reactionary organizations anyway and says it would fight for a Congress seat.
game_relevance: An organization's class derives from who its members are (wage-floor covered or not, productive sector or not), so one union-type organization can be aristocratic in one county and proletarian in another. The player's organization can enter reactionary organizations as tactics without changing its class line.

citations.quote: Fighting union struggles in the united $tates --with the exception of immigrant, migrant and prisoner unions-- only leads to a further crackdown
replacing the old leaders by Communists in proletarian organisations of absolutely every type
If we could win a Congress seat, we would fight for it.

claim: What elections can change, in MIM's account: the work of social democrats 'never succeeds' and at its best 'turns the oppressed into oppressor'; MIM says only whites in their majority voted for Bush, reading the electorate as exploiter-dominated; the task for the oppressed inside the US is 'peaceful and legal' work, not armed struggle.
game_relevance: The electorate (legal working rights, citizens) and the in-border proletariat (undocumented, incarcerated) are nearly disjoint by construction, so an election cannot express the proletariat's choice. An electoral system in the game needs a franchise attribute, and a ballot result should read as a contest inside the aristocracy and petty-bourgeoisie.

citations.quote: The work of social-democrats never succeeds, but when it is most effective it turns the oppressed into oppressor instead of abolishing both
Since only whites in their majority voted for Bu$h

citations.locator: B.4, paragraph beginning 'It is not yet the turn'
citations.quote: Our work should be peaceful and legal as Mao suggested

tension: An earlier reader recorded 'Don't vote, organize' (not repeated here); MIM also says it would hold a Congress seat, so its line is not abstention in the abstract. 'What an election can and cannot change' is a design call that needs the Director.

claim: Borders and labor supply: MIM says the imperialist country has no free market in labor-power because borders are closed 'through alliance with the labor aristocracy', and that aristocratic politics targets migrants even though the aristocracy's Social Security and Medicaid depend on the age mix of migrant workers.
game_relevance: Labor supply is segmented: a legal pool under a wage floor and a controlled migrant/undocumented pool outside it. County migration and hiring rules should be able to open or close the second pool; the aristocracy's age mix creates a demographic dependency on it.

citations.quote: their borders are closed through alliance with the labor aristocracy. The free market for labor-power in the imperialist country is eliminated.
even though the solvency of the labor aristocracy's Social Security and Medicaid programs is at stake, because of the shortage of the right age of workers.

tension: PER-32 requires employed + reserve = labor force with mortality, migration and inactivity explicit; a segmented-pool reading needs a legal-status split inside that count.

claim: The labor aristocracy's size is bounded and self-undermining in MIM's account: its expansion 'must reach a limit set by the surplus-value that can be extracted' globally; growth of unproductive labor coincides with a falling profit rate (Shaikh and Tonak); job multipliers differ by sector (100 new manufacturing jobs create 422 others; personal and business services 147; retail 94). MIM's capital-output ratio table (1950 / mid / 1989 columns) shows rises in France, Germany, Japan and the UK, while the US reads 2.26, 2.06, 2.24, i.e. roughly flat with a dip.
game_relevance: A bounded, endogenous aristocratic share of employment tied to imported-goods surplus-value gives a mechanism that can reverse. Sector job multipliers (from Greider 1997) are a calibration for how many unproductive jobs a productive job supports.

citations.quote: Hence, a key Leninist proposition is that the expansion of the labor aristocracy must reach a limit set by the surplus-value that can be extracted
An expansion of manufacturing employment by 100 results in the creation of 422 other jobs
the expansion of the proportion of unproductive laborers in the United $tates coincides with a decline in the rate of profit

verification_note: Quotes found; 147 and 94 multipliers confirmed. The capital-output row is 2.26 / 2.06 / 2.24 (column headers not re-checked here), so 'stayed flat' was narrowed. Attribution of the job multipliers to Greider 1997 was not checked.

claim: The aristocracy consumes and owns the superprofit: MIM says workers 'take up luxury consumption with their wages' and 'many workers manage to buy their monopoly capitalist corporations' (airlines, car rental, groceries); in Japan 97 percent of firms have employee stock programs and in 21 percent workers are among the top ten shareholders.
game_relevance: Employee ownership and pension stakes put a worker cohort and an owner company on both sides of the account; company owner and treasury accounts need cohort shareholders so one cohort can draw wages and also receive profit.

citations.quote: many workers manage to buy their monopoly capitalist corporations, as some airlines, car-rental and grocery chain stores are in the United $tates.
97 percent of firms have employee stock-ownership programs and in 21 percent of firms, workers rank in the top ten shareholders.

claim: The lumpenproletariat in the BPP/MIM account: Mao's lumpen are 'brave fighters but apt to be destructive' who 'can become a revolutionary force if given proper guidance'. Newton and Cleaver expected a majority to descend from the petty-bourgeoisie into the lumpen (automation, prison); MIM does not adopt a lumpen-majority line but notes the 'prison craze', and says it organizes for the lumpen and undocumented because the revolutionary classes have no majority inside US borders.
game_relevance: Lumpen and undocumented cohorts are the groups whose alignment is contested by organizations, and prison and unemployment inflows are the downward-mobility channel in this frame. The player's organization competes for these cohorts more than for the aristocratic majority.

citations.quote: Brave fighters but apt to be destructive, they can become a revolutionary force if given proper guidance.
The Black Panthers said it would take the descent into the lumpen from the petty-bourgeoisie to create a revolutionary majority.
MIM has not put forward the line of an emerging lumpen majority.

claim: Strategic frame: MIM says the Third World proletariat is the main force of revolution 'even in the case of the United $tates', that it 'is not yet the turn' of oppressed nations inside the US to start armed struggle, and that the task inside borders is 'long, slow and detailed' rear-area work. It also warns against protectionist and nationalist demands among the aristocracy because they lead to fascism and inter-imperialist war.
game_relevance: The player's in-border project is organizing and reform inside a world system the engine sees only through trade and migration flows; a revolutionary victory on the US map is not an expected outcome of cohort choice alone. A design that makes 'revolution' reachable from US class choices alone departs from the MIM line.

citations.quote: we at MIM believe that the Third World proletariat is the main force of revolution, even in the case of the United $tates and other imperialist countries.

citations.locator: B.4, paragraph beginning 'It is not yet the turn'
citations.quote: It is not yet the turn of the oppressed nations within the belly of the beast to start the armed struggle.

tension: The Constitution keeps geography fixed and NORTH_STAR says the player can pursue an electoral, reformist or revolutionary project with direction from practice. MIM's line makes the revolutionary branch largely exogenous to US cohort choices; this needs the Director.

claim: Places where the MIM line forces a concrete design choice: (1) the default class of a US wage-earning cohort is labor aristocracy (petty-bourgeois), proletarian only if undocumented, incarcerated or lumpen; (2) class comes from a sign test on net transfer while nation comes from declared incidence, and the two stay separate axes on every group; (3) the electorate (legal working rights) and the in-border proletariat are nearly disjoint, so elections move aristocratic and petty-bourgeois cohorts and cannot represent the proletariat; (4) the superprofit term is imports times a calibrated multiplier (8 to 10), classed Calibrated and shown as such; (5) class hardens with time and reverses only when the transfer shrinks, with no threshold constant; (6) organizations take their class from their members; (7) a revolutionary outcome is not reachable from US cohort choices alone.
game_relevance: Lists the forks that need confirmation before a class-agent model is built. Items 1-3 and 7 change play most; 4 and 5 touch the Constitution's rules on calibrated values and curves.

citations.quote: it is impossible to see any proletariat where there is an imperialist country minimum wage in effect.
There is no proletariat among people with legal working rights.
we at MIM believe that the Third World proletariat is the main force of revolution, even in the case of the United $tates and other imperialist countries.

tension: Items 3 and 7 bear on NORTH_STAR ('electoral, reformist or revolutionary project; direction emerges from practice'). The Director's ruling settles the analytic reading; whether the game makes revolution unreachable by US cohorts is a design decision, not a source fact.

not_found: MCU (Maoist Communist Union): no text in the MIM corpus. The only hits for 'MCU' are an unrelated prison Management Control Unit. MIM says nothing about it, so no claim is made about its line from this corpus.

The term 'First Worldism' / 'First Worldist': no hits in /media/user/data/mim/etext. MIM's own terms are labor aristocracy, white-nation, parasitism, bribed workers and mythology of the white proletariat.

The Freedom Road Socialist Organization's own documents are not in the MIM corpus except the 1985 Principles of Unity as MIM's critique quotes it (noisy OCR). Passages quoted in mim-fr-unity.pdf are too corrupted to quote cleanly beyond two fragments.

MIM Theory issues 4, 8, 10, 11, 12 are cited as the places with MIM's full reviews of Workers World, the CPUSA, DSA origins and FRSO (MT12). Those articles were not located as text, only referenced by title in the MIM directory pages.
MIM material on the Rainbow Coalition or Jackson campaigns as a separate analysis: only passing mentions found.
A separate MIM essay specifically on the ISO or Solidarity beyond the one-line directory entries.
gaps: 1) Locators are tag-stripped non-empty line numbers (or section names), not raw file line numbers. 2) mim-3rd-draft.pdf is the same text as MIM.essays/critique.of.rcp (dated 1986-87, before MIM's 1987 turn), and I cited the HTML copy because the PDF OCR is noisy. 3) mim-fr-unity.pdf is mostly unreadable OCR, so the FRSO position there rests on two short fragments (low confidence). 4) MIM's numerical claims (surplus value under $500 billion, 50th-percentile income, 3.5 million capitalists) come from 1990-94 Statistical Abstract figures that I did not recheck, so they remain unchecked, as does MIM's claim that the RCP is a CIA front. 5) FRSO, CPUSA, WWP and DSA are characterized only through MIM's accounts and a few quotes. Their own offers should be checked against their own texts before being written as game content. 6) I did not read MIM Theory issues, the RCP Draft Programme, Sakai's Settlers, or the Edwards labor aristocracy text, which carry MIM's full analysis. 7) Not covered: MIM's criticism of anarchists, ultraleft council communists, Stalinist/Hoxhaist groups and the Black nationalist organizations beyond one line each, and MIM's lumpen position.
verifier_notes: All 70+ quotes were machine-checked against the cited files with whitespace, tag and entity normalization. All were found, after correcting one spelling in deng.html ('Self-Description :'). Corrections made: F08 locators loosened because the file is hard-wrapped; F15 locator moved to roughly lines 322-331 and a 1987 quote added; F17 narrowed because the no-Western-use claim is not shown by the citations; F20 'feel-good subjectivist' attributed to subreform.html and MN129 dated 1 Jan 1997; F22 AIFLD and Trotskyists text is in a different 1996 resolution from resolution 15. Several secondary details inside claims were not individually checked and are flagged in the verification_notes, notably the F21 MC6 and 1987 attribution, F11's ISO and multiracial details, and F25's WWP index-page claim. Nothing was dropped.

claim: MIM's own test for choosing between itself and the RCP is one class-reading question: is the majority of the US population exploited, or bought off and parasitic? MIM says it does not want members who hold the exploited reading, though such people may work with it. This is MIM's central dividing line against every organization to its right. MIM's page lists it as the touchstone against the RCP, and the 1996 congress and the MIM Notes 129 critique of FRSO apply the same test to other lines. The page is undated, but it is the post-1987 line.
game_relevance: Every rival organization needs an explicit 'class reading of the US wage-earning cohort' attribute (exploited vs bribed/parasitic). That attribute is what separates the player's MIM-line organization from the RCP, CPUSA, DSA, Trotskyists and FRSO-type groups. It should drive whom each organization targets and which demands it makes.
tension: NORTH_STAR says residents can share a class position and still choose different organizations. A party that screens members on this reading is an organization-level rule and must not become a rule on cohorts. The engine must still judge outcomes from material accounts, not from the label.

citations.locator: tag-stripped non-empty lines 2-6 (MIM answer: difference between MIM and the RCP-USA)
citations.quote: If you believe that the majority of the population within U.$. borders is bought-off, petty-bourgeoisie and parasitic, then you should join

claim: MIM defines the labor aristocracy as the working class that benefits from imperialist superexploitation of the Third World. Of white US workers it says that, as a class, they are no longer exploited. Because the benefit has lasted long enough, it says they should be called petty-bourgeoisie, not workers. This is MIM's general class term for the base of every rival line in F08-F17.
game_relevance: A US wage-earning cohort's default class reading under the game's line is 'labor aristocracy / petty-bourgeoisie', not 'proletariat'. Whether a given cohort is exploited stays an account-level outcome: wage versus value, with the sign of the balance. Rival organizations then differ in whether they flatter or contest that reading.
tension: The MIM-specific claim that white workers as a class are not exploited rests on MIM's own statistical accounting (F03), which is still unchecked. PER-337 forbids inferring political consciousness from aid or provisioning, so the class reading must come from account balances and observed choices, not be asserted per cohort.

citations.locator: Revolutionary Definitions, 'Labor aristocracy' entry (tag-stripped non-empty lines 100-106)
citations.quote: white workers in the United States benefit from the superexploitation of the Third World so greatly, that as a class, they are no longer exploited at all
are not workers anymore, but petty-bourgeoisie.

claim: In its 1994 review of Workers World, MIM argues from US Statistical Abstract figures that surplus value extracted by capitalists is at most a few hundred billion dollars a year. It says that this can be accounted for by discrimination against workers of color and by Third World labor, and that no net surplus value comes from white workers as a class. These are MIM's own calculations from 1990-1993 data. I did not recheck them against the sources, so they are unchecked.
game_relevance: Do not hard-code 'white workers are unexploited' as a constant. The engine should compute value, wage and balance from its own accounts, and it can be checked whether the MIM reading holds in those accounts. A rival organization's claim of 'exploitation of the white working class' can then be tested against the same accounts.
tension: The Constitution requires every substantive value to be classed Observed, Derived, Calibrated or Designed, so MIM's dollar figures cannot be imported as constants. This is also the 'findings still marked unchecked' case.

citations.quote: There is no way to see any net surplus-value coming from white workers as a class.

claim: Workers World Party in 1994 demanded a $10 minimum wage. MIM refuses that demand, saying it only stokes the chauvinism of US workers, who will deal with imperialism to share in Third World exploitation. MIM puts redistribution to the Third World first. The only version it would back is $10 as a maximum wage. It says this as a thought experiment ('space aliens'), not as a program.
game_relevance: A WWP-type rival organization offers wage and jobs demands that attract low-wage and unemployed US cohorts. FPLmimp.pdf was read for class, strands, reform and error sections, pp.4-6, 10, 13, 17, 19, 30, 34, 58-60. I did not read MIM Theory 1 (mt1.pdf) for the labor-aristocracy argument or any of MT5 and MT9 on line, strategy and tactics. MIM Theory 11 BPP (mt11bpp.html) and the lumpen and prisoner line were left to the earlier reader. verifier_notes:
I checked all 31 findings against the sources and dropped none. No quote was fabricated, but 15 findings needed narrowing or correction.

Text sources (etext html and txt, NORTH_STAR.md): every quote was found by rg. Several were line-wrapped.

PDFs: FPLmimp.pdf was searched page by page with whitespace and hyphens normalized (non-layout pdftotext), because the two-column layout breaks plain searches. mim-docs.pdf is OCR, with MIM garbled as '(RIM)', and the cited passages were found there. mim-gender.pdf is scanned images, so I viewed PDF pp.88-89 directly. Those pages confirm the F11 and F12 quotes.

The main corrections:
- **Attribution (F02, F03, F22):** the focoism, 'military over-extended' and 'armed revolution cannot be a serious question yet' arguments come from the prisoner Lord Grim's MIM Notes 195 article. MIM only adds an editorial note, and the stage list is cited from MT7 p.16.
- **Locators (F19, F25, F29, F30):** FPLmimp page numbers and line numbers were fixed.
- **Narrowed claims (F25, F27):** sub-claims I could not find in the sources were removed. For F25 these were haste, closing membership and a mid-1969 united front. For F27 they were MIM opposing democracy in principle, petty-bourgeois discontent with both parties, and Black voters following nation.
- **Inference marked (F07, F16):** 'MIM does not treat service use as agreement' (F07) and 'MIM gives no route to revolution from a lost bribe' (F16) are the reader's inferences, not in the quotes.

Game-relevance text was left alone except where flagged. I did not individually check some sub-claims, for example the Panthers saying the breakfast program was not reform (F06). Their verification_notes say so.

claim: MIM's principal task for an imperialist country is two linked outputs: create public opinion, and build independent institutions of the oppressed, in order to seize power. Anything that ranks above that task is an error in practice. 'Discrediting the state as it exists' is the stated content of the task. Charity and demonstrations are by-products of it, not the goal.
game_relevance: The default win-state of a MIM-line organization is two accumulating stocks (reach/legitimacy and its own institutions), not seats or members. Cohort choices (read, attend, join, use a service) should feed those two stocks.
