claim: MIM states four strategic stages for North America: (1) NOW, create public opinion and independent institutions; (2) a qualitative leap to armed struggle for state power, after power has accumulated in stage 1; (3) a short New Democracy with dictatorship of the oppressed nations over the oppressor nation; (4) separate dictatorships of the proletariat inside the oppressed nations and a joint dictatorship over the Euro-Amerikan nation. The sentence that armed revolution is not a serious question until stage 1 is done is the argument of the prisoner author Lord Grim, not a MIM statement.
game_relevance: The player's organization starts at stage 1 and the game should not offer armed struggle as a working path early. Stage labels should be read off accumulated institutions and opinion, never set by a timer.
tension: The project rule 'no threshold constant' means stage 2 cannot be a fixed trigger. Show it as a descriptive label for an emergent state (see F27).

citations.locator: line 43 (quoting MIM Theory 7 p.16, footnote 8; reprinted in MIM Notes 195, mn/mn195/focoism.txt)
citations.quote: NOW: Create public opinion and independent institutions of the people to prepare to seize power.
This stage includes dictatorship of the oppressed nations over the oppressor nation.

verification_note: Both quotes found, and the four-stage text is attributed to MIM Theory 7 p.16 by the article's footnote. The claim 'armed revolution cannot be a serious question until stage 1 is realized' is Lord Grim's own wording, printed in MIM Notes 195 with a MIM editorial note that does not repeat it. Narrowed the claim to say so.

claim: MIM treats the revolutionary opening as set largely by the world conjuncture, not by domestic organizing alone. MIM(Prisons) writes that revolution in the US comes as the military is over-extended abroad. The MIM Notes 195 article (by a prisoner, Lord Grim, quoting the pamphlet What is MIM p.11 and a Weatherman quote) says victory in the US will be made 'by the people of the whole world'.
game_relevance: An organization cannot manufacture a revolutionary situation by its own activity. Openings should come from engine-computed external pressure (war, imperial overextension), and an organization's stocks decide whether it can use one.
tension: Babylon holds geography fixed and the national campaign is a domestic circuit. Nothing in the live loop carries an imperial-overextension signal yet.

citations.quote: Revolution will become a reality within the United $tates as the military becomes over-extended

citations.locator: MIM Notes 195, 'On Focoism and the Lumpen Proletariat' (author Lord Grim)
citations.quote: Victorious armed revolution will be possible when the oppressors are weak in the Amerikan imperialist state.

verification_note: FPLmimp p.4 quote found exactly. The mn195 quote is found but is the prisoner author's sentence, which he supports with a Weatherman quote that 'What is MIM' p.11 reproduces; MIM only appends a note. The 'MIM tells its own cadre to expect the opening and to prepare, not to wait on any class' part is an inference, though F15's 'will not wait for any strata' supports half of it. Confidence lowered to medium and attribution fixed.

claim: MIM's own organizational model has three tiers with different obligations: the party (cadre), a mass organization (RAIL) with 'limited obligations of discipline' that focuses on public opinion, and an 'army' that gives concrete and logistical support to the institutions of the oppressed. Recruits enter through the mass organization first, and the mass organization is recruited to anti-imperialism before Maoism.
game_relevance: Cohorts need not choose between 'join the party' and nothing. A funnel of contact, mass-organization member and cadre gives bounded choices, with different time, risk and discipline at each level. This fits NORTH_STAR's 'decline to join one'.

citations.quote: RAIL members acknowledge party leadership like the army, but RAIL members are under limited obligations of discipline and they focus their work on building public opinion.
All people we meet will be RAIL recruits before they are MIM recruits
recruiting people to anti imperialism first rather than chasing people away by insisting that everyone be a Maoist

claim: MIM sets a fixed time budget for cadre. Every member must put 10 hours a week into mass contact, 5 of them in a recruiting role. Study is organized only for those already doing work. A member is expected to be able to restart the party alone.
game_relevance: Cadre hours per period are a finite stock that an organization splits between contact, study and institution work. This matches the 'finite time' rule and gives the player a real allocation choice.

citations.quote: All MCs must have 10 hours per week of contact with the masses.
ability and desire to restart the party from scratch if every other single member were gone

claim: MIM's 'independent institutions' are Serve-the-People programs that meet needs and organize against imperialism at the same time. MIM(Prisons) frames Mao's Red Army base areas as 'dual power': prototype socialist relations built before taking the state. The Panther breakfast program is the model, and the Panthers said it was not reform.
game_relevance: An institution an organization runs (a clinic, a free-books or food program) is both a material service and a stock of independence from the state. A cohort that uses it gets a real material gain and a tie to the organization. The tie is not consciousness (see F07).

citations.quote: Following in the footsteps of the Black Panther Party, MIM and these institutions simultaneously meet the Peoples needs while organizing against imperialism.
the Red Army built base areas that prototyped socialist relations of production and culture as a form of dual power
Feed the youth and they will feed the revolution.

claim: MIM ranks charity and aid as subordinate: relief is temporary, and a large effect of its work is that people who do not agree with MIM go and support charities instead. MIM does not treat service use as agreement.
game_relevance: A cohort that uses an organization's aid should not be marked as politically aligned with it. This agrees with the PER-337 rule never to infer consciousness from aid or provisioning, and MIM's own line supports the rule.

citations.locator: p.7 (OCR, about line 394-411 of extracted text)
citations.quote: believes that as a strategy charity can never provide more than temporary and limited relief.

verification_note: Quote found in OCR text (MIM appears garbled as '(RIM)'). The same passage says charity is done 'as a subordinate aspect of our work to create public opinion ... as a by-product', and that people who disagree with MIM support charities instead. The final sentence 'does not treat service use as agreement' is an inference, not stated. Marked as such.

claim: MIM's answer to 'who can be organized' inside the US: the oppressed nations are the base. The Euro-Amerikan working class is a labor aristocracy and not objectively allied with proletarian revolution. The class enemy beyond the imperialists is the labor aristocracy. Union leaders are its most dangerous section. Individuals can commit 'class suicide', but as a group the labor aristocracy will not join now.
game_relevance: Default recruitment odds for a US wage-earning cohort in the dominant nation are low for a revolutionary organization. The individual-versus-group split can be modelled as a small tail of individual defectors inside a cohort whose group tendency runs against the organization.
tension: NORTH_STAR says residents can share a class position and choose differently. MIM allows that only as an individual tail, not a group tendency. Recruitment, and not only the class label, must stay account-driven.

citations.locator: p.30 (MIM Theory 2/3, Summer 1992, p.81, section I.B-D)
citations.quote: These individuals can commit class suicide and join the revolution. As a group they will not do this now.
the masses of Euro-Amerikan people are not objectively allied with proletarian revolution.
the union leaders are the most dangerous of these enemies

claim: MIM says the petty-bourgeoisie 'could go either way' and that conditions decide. In the imperialist countries today its interest is allied with the bourgeoisie because of shared imperialist wealth. The same conditional logic runs through MIM's class reading: alignment follows material interest at the time, not a fixed label.
game_relevance: Alignment should be computed from each cohort's material margin (income relative to the value of its labor, ownership, dependency). A cohort whose margin collapses is the only one MIM treats as movable as a group.

citations.quote: Conditions determine which way they go as a group, and in imperialist countries today their material interests are allied with the bourgeoisie

claim: MIM names the labor aristocracy as a lower segment of the petty-bourgeoisie: wage earners who earn more than the value of their labor, with no means to start a business. 'In the First World this group is not exploited.' It also defines 'majority-exploiter countries' as at least 51% bourgeoisie in population, and the list includes the United $tates.
game_relevance: This forces the default class reading of a US wage-earning cohort: not proletarian by default. The reading must be derived per cohort from wages against value of labor, and cannot be a flat occupation label.
tension: ADR171's bribe-versus-deprivation masses (1.55x) are a project-checked derivation. MIM's 51% figure and the 'earn more than the value of their labor' test are MIM assertions. They are not verified here and need the engine's own value measure. Intensive quantities must not be averaged across classes.

citations.quote: In the First World this group is not exploited and so not part of the proletariat.
countries that are at least 51% bourgeoisie in population

claim: MIM's first-class dimensions for every group are three strands: nation, class and gender. Nation is the principal contradiction on the world scale and within US borders. Gender is a secondary oppression in total, with no strand for lesbian and gay rights. In MIM's 1991 debate, naming nation as principal does more for class and gender than naming either of them.
game_relevance: Every population group carries a nation attribute that cannot be dropped, since nation decides who can be organized into which alliance. Class and gender are further dimensions. Gender appears in MIM's strand theory but not in NORTH_STAR, so it needs a Director decision before it is added.
tension: Gender has no material account in the current model: MIM defines the gender aristocracy by sexual privilege. The Constitution requires a material relation for each formal element, so this stays unadopted until a material relation is named.

citations.quote: Within U.$. borders, the principal contradiction is between imperialism and the oppressed nations.
We do not even have a secondary strand of oppression for gay rights and we believe that the total of gender oppression is a secondary oppression.

citations.locator: PDF p.89, printed p.88 (MIM Theory 2/3, 'Class as a candidate for principal contradiction in the United States', MC5, 10 Nov 1991)
citations.quote: Picking the right principal contradiction is essential to taking the fastest road forward.

claim: MIM's rule for the oppressed nations: nationalism has a dual character, revolutionary in the oppressed nation and reactionary in the dominant one. The oppressed nations' struggle is an alliance of working masses with the left wing of the national bourgeoisie and sections of the petty bourgeoisie. The proletarian share of leadership decides how revolutionary it is. Inside the Black, Latino and Indigenous nations, class struggle is 'rarely, if ever' the principal contradiction.
game_relevance: A group's alignment is its nation's alliance structure first. Within an oppressed nation the engine should not play class split against national unity as the main axis. A group's revolutionary potential rises with the proletarian ideology's share of leadership in the national alliance.
tension: MIM's national alliance picture is richer than the three named nations in ADR171. Overlap policy and non-contiguity stay as ruled. Do not add a nation without the Director.

citations.quote: Their struggle is the revolutionary nationalist struggle, comprising an alliance of the working masses with the left-wing of the national bourgeoisie and sections of the petty bourgeoisie
It appears that within the Black, Latino and Indigenous nations, class struggle is rarely, if ever, the principal contradiction.

claim: MIM's stated dual purpose is to divide the dominant nation by drawing off potentially revolutionary elements, 'students and young people', and to build united Maoist leadership of the oppressed nations. It treats division of the oppressor nation as a revolutionary development and division of an oppressed nation as a setback.
game_relevance: Winning and losing groups are asymmetric. An organization gains by splitting dominant-nation cohorts (especially the young) and loses by splitting oppressed-nation cohorts. Opponents (the state, employers) have the opposite incentive.

citations.quote: seeking to divide the dominant Amerikan nation by drawing off members of such potentially revolutionary elements as students and young people
The division of the oppressor nations is a revolutionary development, while the division of the oppressed nations represents a setback and loss for the people's struggle against imperialism.

claim: MIM treats youth as a stratum rather than a class, so 'any strata can lead the revolution'. It also holds that most Amerikan youth are not revolutionary because it is against their material interests, and that within the Euro-Amerikan nation the principal contradiction is age. The 'stratum' essay is a 1980s third draft, before the labor-aristocracy line was formalized.
game_relevance: Age bands in the household lifecycle (under 16, 16-17, 18-64, 65+) are meaningful organizing categories. Young cohorts in the dominant nation are the most movable group, but their default pull is toward imperialist wealth. A youth-facing organization needs a material basis, and a message alone will not move them.
tension: The 'any strata can lead' essay predates MT1. MIM(Prisons) says older etext documents can contradict later developments (F26), so treat the age-as-principal-contradiction claim as the later line and the stratum claim as an early one.

citations.quote: Precisely because youth do not form a class but a strata, they can lead revolution.
Most Amerikan youth are not revolutionary because it is against their material interests to be revolutionary.
the principal contradiction in the Euro-Amerikan nation today is in age

verification_note: All three quotes exist (wrapped across lines; the floridahampers one spans lines 64-65 with the sentence starting on 63). The essay is headed 'THIRD DRAFT' and refers to 1984 and 1986 sources, supporting the 1980s dating. The paraphrase 'any strata can lead the revolution' is not verbatim; the source says youth can lead because they are a strata. Locator for floridahampers fixed to 63-65.

claim: MIM says its social base comes from its line on imperialism and war, not from class struggle inside the US. 'MIM will not wait for any strata or the proletariat itself.' This is an early (about 1986) formulation. Later MIM says the First World majority are not an objective ally.
game_relevance: Who an organization can recruit follows from the organization's line plus its material offer, and population composition does not by itself fix it. A group is not 'the base' because of its census class.
tension: The essay predates MT1 and the later ruling that the white working class is a labor aristocracy. Use it only for the 'line decides base' rule, not for its class claims.

citations.quote: MIM's social base is that group of people who see the necessity of destroying and transcending imperialism
MIM will not wait for any strata or the proletariat itself to mount the political stage.

claim: MIM's picture of what moves the labor aristocracy as a group is nationalist and fascist, not revolutionary. When the bribe seems too small it 'turns to economic nationalism' and would break away only to ultra-nationalist groups. MIM Theory 10 reads 1968 as the Panthers' lumpen alliance and vanguard discipline 'repelling' Euro-Amerikan workers, who would have followed middle-class ideology as French workers did. MIM states no route by which loss of the bribe turns the labor aristocracy revolutionary.
game_relevance: A dominant-nation cohort whose margin falls should tend toward chauvinist or fascist organizations, not toward the revolutionary one. That agrees with the earlier project finding that balance sign feeds a fascism-versus-revolution bifurcation. Only imperial defeat or war (F03) changes the structure.
tension: MIM states the drop-in-the-bribe case, while the project memory states the positive-balance case. Both end in chauvinism, but the memory finding needs rechecking before it is cited for MIM. Escalation must stay rank-order under a budget, with no threshold constant.

citations.quote: When the labor aristocracy feels that the imperialists aren't giving it enough of the booty from international profits, it complains and turns to economic nationalism.
If the labor aristocracy is going to break away for an alternative soon, it will be to break away to these ultra-nationalist groups to try to restore the empire to its appropriate glory.
the high profile of the Black Panthers, the alliance with the lumpen element and disciplined vanguard organization all repelled the Euro-Amerikan workers.

verification_note: All three quotes found (the first two wrap across lines). The mt10bpp passage says the workers of France followed a middle-class ideology and that Euro-Amerikan workers would have too. Both the 'MIM gives no route' sentence and the 'fascist' label are the reader's inference from absence and are not in the quotes; marked as interpretation within a source_fact entry.

claim: MIM's line on unions and wage struggle: union struggle inside the US 'only leads to a further crackdown' on exploited workers elsewhere, except immigrant, migrant and prisoner unions. Rightist economism is cheerleading wage struggles as tantamount to revolution. MIM also says the union leaders are the most dangerous enemy section of the labor aristocracy.
game_relevance: A workplace committee or union in a labor-aristocracy workforce is not an organizing win by default. Immigrant, migrant and prisoner organizing are the exceptions. Wage gains for a labor-aristocratic cohort should not raise its revolutionary alignment, and may entrench it.
tension: NORTH_STAR names a workplace committee in the live Wayne County group set. MIM's line says its meaning depends on whose workers they are. Do not treat any union as automatically progressive.

citations.quote: Fighting union struggles in the united $tates --with the exception of immigrant, migrant and prisoner unions-- only leads to a further crackdown on other WHITE workers exploited in the ex-Soviet bloc and Central Asia.
Rightist economists cheerlead for wage struggles as tantamount to revolution.

claim: MIM's criteria for when a reform demand is progressive: it is a 'winnable battle' that wins some resources, exposes the state's cruelty, and is led by revolutionaries. Revolutionaries should unite with and lead reform battles but should not join liberal single-issue organizations, which dilute them. Reform work 'more often' shows that reforms do not work.
game_relevance: A reform campaign has three outcomes to score: material relief for the cohort, exposure of the state, and the organization's own independence. A campaign scores well for a MIM-line organization only if it keeps independence and feeds the opinion stock. Reform alone does not.
tension: NORTH_STAR names a reformist project as a legitimate player path. Under MIM's framework the engine should simply score reform by these material effects, with no label attached.

citations.locator: p.60 ('Looking Left', USW study group on MIM Theory 5)
citations.quote: Revolutionaries work on reforms because some do improve the lives of people on a small scale, yet more often our work on reform battles further confirms that reforms do not work
revolutionaries should not join liberal mass organizations because they will eventually be forced to water down their politics for the sake of the single-issue organization
we fight winnable battles against things like prison repression, police brutality and other reactionary policies.

claim: MIM's united-front rules, as applied by its mass organization: keep ideological and organizational independence; do not demand that allies give up theirs; agree points of unity per event; do not admit groups led by revisionists; and a united front is 'a proletarian-led broad mobilization of various classes'. MIM(Prisons) says who to unite with is a strategic question that changes with the stage of struggle.
game_relevance: Alliances between organizations are bounded and event-specific, with leadership kept distinct. This suits a negotiation or coalition mechanic where groups hold their own identity and an organization cannot absorb its partners.

citations.quote: RAIL will not give up its ideological or organizational independence
A successful United Front is a proletarian-led broad mobilization of various classes and interests.
who to form united fronts with is really a strategic question, as the answer may change as the strategic stage of struggle changes.

verification_note: Quotes found. Locator for FPLmimp fixed from pp.13-14 to p.14 (text located on page 14). The sub-claims about points of unity per event and excluding revisionist-led groups were not separately checked against whatisrail.html.

claim: MIM's 'mass practice' is a feedback loop: understand the conditions of the people, pick the most accessible tactical battle, act, then change practice from the people's criticism. Practice is tied to the people most oppressed (prisoners) before rallies and publicity.
game_relevance: An organization's effectiveness with a group depends on how well it reads that group's material conditions and responds to results. This suggests an information quality measure: an organization that never samples its base mis-targets campaigns.

citations.quote: Mass practice is understanding the conditions of the people, understanding which tactical battles are most important at a given time, and taking action to oppose the most accessible aspects of imperialism.

claim: MIM names right opportunism as the main danger in the imperialist countries: tailing spontaneous struggle and saying what people want to hear. 'Liberal opportunism' (working with everyone, losing direction) is more common than sectarianism, which MIM defines as putting the organization's own needs above the international proletariat. First World organizations with a large following 'stand for bourgeois ideals'.
game_relevance: Two named failure modes for in-game organizations: rightist drift from catering to a majority, and sectarianism from refusing to unite. Membership size is not a success measure for a First-World organization and may indicate drift.
tension: A plain 'more members is better' score would contradict MIM. NORTH_STAR says labels do not predetermine success, so the drift should come from what the organization's messages and offers do to its membership, not from a label.

citations.quote: This "right opportunism" is the main danger in the party-building process in the world.
an organization puts its own needs above those of the international proletariat
if you're an organization in the First World and have a large following you stand for bourgeois ideals.

claim: MIM names focoism as the main ultra-left error: small armed cells creating revolutionary conditions by example. MIM's editorial note says its failures come from the wrong line, and that a focoist has 'significant disagreements' with Marxism-Leninism-Maoism. The article's author Lord Grim (not MIM itself) argues that premature armed action worsens revolution's prospects through backlash, and separates armed self-defense (acceptable) from armed struggle for revolution (premature now). MC5 in MIM Theory 7 p.55 names refusing repetitive revolutionary tasks in favor of big glorious battles as liberalism.
game_relevance: Adventurism has a computable cost: a premature armed action raises state repression on the organization's institutions and members and cannot be recovered quickly. Armed self-defense is a separate action with a different payoff.

citations.locator: MIM Notes 195, 'On Focoism and the Lumpen Proletariat' (quoting What is MIM p.11)
citations.quote: Focoism is a popular theory that says that small cells of armed revolutionaries can create the conditions for revolution through their actions.
we consider that person to have some significant disagreements with Marxism-Leninism-Maoism

citations.locator: MC5 quoted from MIM Theory 7 p.55 (footnote 5)
citations.quote: The failure to carry out repetitive tasks necessary for the revolution is an example of liberalism.

verification_note: All three quotes found (the first is in the single-line file, so the locator is by article). Attribution fixed: the definition is quoted from What is MIM p.11; the backlash and self-defense arguments are Lord Grim's, with MIM's added note covering 'failure of line'. Not changed otherwise.

claim: MIM names 'left' economism and commandism: oscillating between treating the masses as asses and expecting them to rise to a heroic example. It results in personality cult, a stifling division of labor, commandism and attacks on the masses. Right economism is waiting for economic conditions to hand over revolutionaries, especially through wage struggles. MIM(Prisons) adds ultra-leftism (moral purity over strategy) and liquidationism (turning all energy to mass organizations with largely petty-bourgeois projects).
game_relevance: These give a list of computable organization failure modes with concrete signatures. Examples: exposure-without-response (masses are asses), wage-struggle-only (economism), purity tests that cost allies (ultra-leftism), mass-organization-only drift away from cadre work (liquidationism).

citations.quote: The masses are asses line results in commandism and attacks on the masses.
waiting for economic conditions to dish up revolutionaries on the silver platter
We say their practice is liquidationist because they turned all their energy to building mass organizations focused on largely petty

claim: MIM says left and right errors are defined relative to conditions: 'what is left and what is right changes as conditions change'. Focoism is ultra-left now, yet armed struggle is a necessity at a later stage. Whether a tactic is an error depends on stage and the assessment of material conditions.
game_relevance: Error modes cannot be fixed tags on an action. 'Armed action' or 'electoral work' is a failure or a success depending on stage and the state of the organization's stocks. This matches the NORTH_STAR rule that labels do not predetermine success.

citations.quote: How we avoid the errors depends on our ability to assess our material conditions, because what is left and what is right changes as conditions change.

claim: MIM's lessons from the Panthers (MT10) for failure modes: state repression coordinated against a visible organization; ultra-democracy and liberalism inside the party, answered by purging; haste. MIM(Prisons) draws a security lesson: stay underground as far as possible, since being above ground helps the repressive apparatus.
game_relevance: Visibility is a trade-off: high-profile growth brings repression. A membership-closed period to raise ideological level is a legitimate organizational choice, not only a failure. The state's response should scale with exposure.

citations.quote: the coordinated and highly modern state repression that Mao warned about in the imperialist countries, but which the Panthers took too lightly
The purges of 1969 followed Mao's advice of combating liberalism and ultrademocracy.
Why should MIM make the job of the repressive apparatus any easier by being completely above ground?

verification_note: All quotes found; the FPLmimp locator was p.58 but the text is on p.59. The original claim added 'haste and expectation of imminent collapse', 'closing membership' and 'a mid-1969 shift to a united front against fascism'; those were not checked against mt10bpp and are removed. The 'membership-closed period is legitimate' game_relevance sentence is the reader's inference.

claim: MIM's line has changed over time, and MIM(Prisons) says so. Older etext documents can contradict later developments. United front is a strategic question, not a cardinal principle; single-nation versus multinational party form is not a dividing line. The Director's ruling that the game's ideology sides with MIM should therefore be read as the current MIM line, with dated early documents used only for what they still support.
game_relevance: Pin each design rule to the latest MIM statement and flag older-draft sources, as F14 and F15 do. Do not mix the 1980s party-building essays with the 1990s-2020s positions.

citations.quote: some older documents in the etext archive represent an earlier stage in MIM's international work and so contradict the more recent developments
The form of organization is not a cardinal question.

claim: MIM's line says elections cannot change the structure but can change local conditions. The capitalists would dissolve a real electoral challenge by military force (Allende's Chile); most progressive reforms came from organizing outside the electoral arena; an elected president, senator, representative or governor 'is not going to make a difference'; only winnable local fights such as public bulletin boards might justify supporting city-hall candidates; oppressed nations vote heavily for Democrats.
game_relevance: Under MIM's line the engine should make an office's decision set bounded: a local office can change local resource and access questions, while military and security structure sits outside it. Votes come from nation and material margin. An organization's electoral win should not by itself raise state power or consciousness.
tension: NORTH_STAR allows an electoral path and says endorsements follow an electoral system that sets who votes, what office is at stake and what its holder can decide. MIM's line does not forbid the path. It predicts limited yield, which the engine should compute and not assume.

citations.quote: dissolve such an election through military force as in Allende's

if there were several candidates running for city hall who supported putting up public bulletin boards all over town and making public space available for revolutionaries to hold educational events, it might be worth supporting them.
most of the progressive reforms won in this country in the past century were the result of organizing and agitation outside of the electoral arena.
Since oppressed nationalities vote heavily for Democrats

verification_note: Quotes found. The mim-docs OCR text reads 'dissolve such an election through military force as in Allende's ...' (the original first citation fragment 'Even if they did, they would dissolve such an election' was not matched as one string). The 'is not going to make a difference' quote is at dontvote.html line 24. Removed unsupported sub-claims: 'MIM opposes democracy in principle where a majority would deny survival rights', 'discontent with both parties is petty-bourgeois', and 'Black voters follow nation' (the last only loosely matches elections012608.html).

claim: MIM treats an unorganized lumpen and proletarian anger as likely to veer into apolitical crime, and says imperialist-country communists must match the people's angry mood to keep it from being wasted. Immigrants, migrants and prisoners are exempt from MIM's critique of union struggle.
game_relevance: A cohort with no organization to receive its anger has a non-political outlet (crime, drug use, despair). This gives lumpen and Third-World-proletarian cohorts a real alternative to joining an organization, so organizing them competes with an outcome and is not a free gain.

citations.quote: veer into apolitical crime if they do not see a party matching its angry mood

claim: MIM (MT7, June 1992) says it is currently a multinational party but would defer to a genuine single-nationality vanguard of an oppressed nationality on organizing that nationality, and that there is no Euro-Amerikan proletariat, so the material basis for a revolutionary Euro-Amerikan party is weak.
game_relevance: Organizations have a nation composition. A cohort of an oppressed nation may prefer an organization led by its own nation, and a dominant-nation cohort is a weak recruiting base. The nation and organization match is a real choice variable.
tension: The overlap policy for Black, Chicano and Indigenous nations is already a ruled design item (ADR171). Single-nation organization is MIM's option, not a settled engine feature.

citations.quote: would defer to such a party on the question of organizing the oppressed nationality in question
there is no Euro-Amerikan proletariat, and the material basis for a revolutionary Euro-Amerikan party is weak.

verification_note: Both quotes found, with locators fixed (the first sits at lines 117-120, the second at about 266-270; the original 259-275 range included both only approximately). The claim was narrowed: the file says MIM recognizes the right of self-determination of such forces, not that it 'lets comrades choose' in the broad sense. Date June 1992 confirmed at line 28.

claim: NORTH_STAR.md (checked-in project rule) treats reformism versus revolution as a central strategic tension and names adventurism and sectarianism as distinct tendencies that develop through practice. It says political labels do not predetermine success or failure, and that residents can share a class position and choose different organizations or decline to join one. MIM's named errors (F21-F25) are consistent with this and supply content for it.
game_relevance: The MIM error list can be implemented as emergent tendencies computed from practice, with no label deciding success. This needs no amendment.

citations.quote: Adventurism and sectarianism are distinct tendencies that can also develop through practice.
Residents can share a class position and choose different organizations or decline to join one.

verification_note: Both passages found; locators adjusted (first sentence begins at line 24 and wraps to 25, the second begins at line 69 and ends at line 71), and the quotes are line-wrapped. Also confirmed the sentence 'Political labels do not predetermine success or failure.' at lines 26-27. That MIM's errors are 'consistent' is the reader's judgment.

claim: Proposed translation of MIM's practice line into bounded choices. Each period a cohort decides, from its own accounts: whether to contact an organization's output (reads, attends), whether to take part in a mass organization at limited discipline, whether to move to cadre work, and whether to use an institution's service. An organization's reach, institutions, discipline and cadre hours determine what it offers. Alignment is computed from the cohort's margin (F09), nation (F12) and what organizations are present, so no label is stored. Failure modes (F21-F25) are computed tendencies from the organization's own record, such as dilution from catering to a majority, premature armed action, or neglected cadre work.
game_relevance: This gives population groups a distinct part in play without making each a full organization, and keeps the choices few and bounded. It fits sparse household cohorts and conserved counts, since the choices change counts of persons and hours, not individual agents.
tension: Must stay inside the Constitution: classify each value Observed, Derived, Calibrated or Designed, and avoid a fixed response curve. Any 'threshold' (for example for tendency onset) would have to be rank-order under a budget.

claim: Gramsci defines the dominant group's hegemony as the spontaneous consent of the masses, caused by the prestige the group has from its function in production, with state coercion held in reserve for groups that do not consent.
game_relevance: A group's willingness to follow an organization should come from that organization's material function for the group (employer wages, union bargaining, state services, a committee's delivered results), plus coercion where consent fails. It should not come from a free-floating message or popularity meter.
tension: Consent from function conflicts with the PER-337 and ADR299 rule that shared provisioning is never evidence of agreement. Resolve it by letting function change the cost or offer a group faces, while consent is recorded only as the group's explicit choices.

claim: Gramsci contrasts war of manoeuvre and war of position. Where civil society is dense, the state is only an outer ditch behind fortresses, and a war of position needs a concentration of hegemony and sacrifice by large masses.
game_relevance: Counties with dense civil society (unions, churches, civic groups, parties) should resist a quick sweeping push and reward patient base-building. A slow campaign should cost the affected groups time and risk each period.

claim: Economism and the economic-corporate stage are Gramsci's failure mode for a movement that only organizes material demands (including treating the party as a trade-union-like educational body). Hegemony must compromise with allied groups but must also be economically grounded. Lenin makes the same point: workers acting by their own effort alone develop only trade-union consciousness.
game_relevance: An organization that only serves bread-and-butter demands can win members without ever becoming a political force, which is a natural 'economism' outcome. Political choices (back a delegate, vote) should need an organizing carrier beyond the workplace, while job-search and moving remain the groups' default economic choices.

claim: Gramsci's organizer is defined by embedded practice (constructor, organiser, permanent persuader), not oratory. He distinguishes democratic centralism ('centralism in movement', thrusts from below matched with orders from above) from bureaucratic centralism. game_relevance: Cadre capacity should come from practice time in the group's daily life, not from broadcast propaganda. Orders that ignore signals from below are a distinct failure (bureaucratic centralism) that should show up as base decay.

a matching of thrusts from below with orders from above

claim: Gramsci treats vote counts as a measurement of an organization's persuasive reach, not a mechanism. Comparing results across levels of election diagnoses cadre quality: strong local but weak higher-level results mean adequate junior cadres but a deficient central leadership.

claim: Two Maoist training texts divide any mass into advanced, intermediate (middle) and backward sections. The method is to unite the advanced to win over the intermediate majority and isolate the backward. The categories are situational, not moral, and the advanced in one phase can become the backward in the next.
game_relevance: Each population group can be represented as three conserved sub-counts (active/advanced, hesitant/middle, resistant/backward), and an organization's cadre time works through the advanced to reach the middle. This stays inside the household-cohort rule because these are counts of persons, not individual agents.
tension: Readiness shares are Designed or Calibrated, never Observed. A second partition (advanced/middle/backward) beside the revolutionary/liberal/fascist ternary risks being a second response curve unless the two are tied by explicit rules.

claim: The Philippine CPP Activist Study names two symmetric errors in mass work. Commandism overestimates the masses' political awareness and violates their voluntary movement. Tailism ties the organization to the larger but backward masses, so it follows instead of leading, even when the advanced and middle are ready and the party is the one needing convincing.
game_relevance: Derive both as outcomes of the gap between what an organization asks of a group and the group's readiness mix. Asks far above the middle's readiness produce commandism (drop-off, resentment). Asks pegged to the backward majority produce tailism (stagnation, advanced leave). No stored label is needed.

claim: MCU's pre-party summation describes a staged contact system. Developing contacts into cadre costs scarce organizational resources, supporters are indispensable, and reorganizing one's life around revolution is no small step.
game_relevance: Membership should be a ladder of costly, separately recorded choices (contact, supporter, member, cadre), each with its own conversion cost in organizer time. Most contacts should plateau as supporters, and many should drop out.

The reactionary leadership has a material basis in privileged strata (the labor aristocracy, a small subsection of the class), union leadership has become a bourgeois profession with staffers, and unions left to themselves degenerate and need a political party to be more than bargaining units.

claim: MIM states its central organizing task as creating public opinion and independent institutions of the oppressed to seize power, and holds that large coalitions led by contradictory leaders or ideologies accomplish nothing. Organization outputs are therefore (a) opinion and (b) standing institutions that groups join.
game_relevance: The competition outputs two things: a shift in the odds a group chooses a given path, and durable institutions (assemblies, committees, mutual-aid bodies). The Wayne claimants' assembly is an early instance of the second and should be generalized, not hand-placed.

claim: MIM defines sectarianism as an organization putting its own needs above the international proletariat's, names liberal opportunism (working together with everyone, no direction) as the opposite error, and says most 'communists' in imperialist countries tend toward liberal opportunism, so opportunism is the main danger. The CPP text names putchism as producing adventurous, destructive actions within the people's army.
game_relevance: Sectarianism and opportunism can be derived from how cadre capacity is split between own growth and coalition work; adventurism from actions that damage unity.

citations.quote: When Marxists speak of "sectarianism," they refer to a situation where an organization puts its own needs above those of the international proletariat.
Liberals and opportunists "work together" with everyone and consequently suffer a lack of direction and get no where.
it means that the "main danger" is opportunism

claim: Althusser lists the political ISA (parties and the political system), the trade union ISA, the family, school, religious, legal, communications and cultural apparatuses as plural, mostly private apparatuses. The repressive apparatus is unified and public. Class struggle inside the ISAs is possible and serious, militants gain their experience there, and each apparatus serves reproduction in its own way under the dominant ideology.
game_relevance: Organizations compete mainly in distinct channels (workplace, union, church, school, media, party), each with different costs and effects, rather than through one propaganda meter. The state's repressive capacity stays one budget (ADR184), while the contestable terrain is the many apparatuses.

citations.quote: while there is one (Repressive) State Apparatus, there is a plurality of Ideological State Apparatuses
In the Ideological State Apparatuses, on the other hand, class struggle is possible, serious, and can go a very long way
Each of them contributes to this single end in its own way.
guaranteeing by force (physical or not) the political conditions for the reproduction of the relations of production

claim: Althusser's interpellation (ideology hails individuals as subjects) operates on individuals, but Babylon has no individual agents. The workable reading is that an organization's message hails a household cohort into a role (claimant, tenant, worker, voter) and offers a recorded choice, with the cohort as the subject.
game_relevance: Implement interpellation as an organization's offer addressed to a group role. The group's accept or decline is the only recorded effect, which preserves the no-individual-agents rule and the rule that agreement is never inferred.
tension: Althusser's 'individuals as subjects' conflicts with the NORTH_STAR rule that the economy does not simulate individual agents. The reading above is my interpretation, not Althusser's.

citations.quote: ideology hails or interpellates individuals as subjects
The Ideological State Apparatuses, in contrast, are infinitely more vulnerable.

claim: Reich argues the thing to explain is non-participation: why most hungry people do not steal and most exploited people do not strike. Economic position is not directly converted into political consciousness, and the average worker is divided, neither clearly revolutionary nor clearly conservative. He also says fascism's mass base was the lower middle class.
game_relevance: Default group behavior should be inaction or no organizational change, and each step into participation needs a cause and a cost. Cohorts should hold divided inclinations rather than one-sided ones, so the same cohort can be pulled by rival organizations.

citations.locator: PDF p.23, 'How Mass Psychology Sees the Problem'

The economic situation is not directly and immediately converted into political consciousness.
the average worker bears a contradiction in himself; that he, in other words, is neither a clear-cut revolutionary nor a clear-cut conservative, but stands divided

claim: Reich and MIM agree that material position does not make workers revolutionary, but their mechanisms differ. Reich puts the cause in character structure formed through the authoritarian family and church, across classes. MIM puts it in the imperialist bribe, saying superprofits buy off whole populations of so-called workers, and that the economic basis of white nationalism, 'left' and fascist, is a bought-off majority.

claim: Mao's 1926 class analysis does not sort the petty bourgeoisie by a fixed label but by material trajectory: those earning a surplus over consumption (aspire upward, fear revolution), those breaking even, and those whose standard of living is falling (the left wing, 'quite important for the revolutionary movement'). Attitude to revolution differs by section in normal times and converges as the revolutionary tide rises.
game_relevance: This is the best operational criterion in the corpus for what a group chooses: a household cohort's class lean follows the sign and trend of its own balance (surplus / break-even / deficit-and-falling), not a static class tag. Cohort accounts already hold income and spending, so a derived 'trajectory' reading is available without a new primitive.
tension: Matches the earlier project finding that the balance sign (not just level) drives direction. Conflicts with any design that assigns a fixed political attitude per class; the same class splits into three sections.
