The relation between ADR171's named nations and a settler or oppressor nation, and the question of whether Asian and Latino cohorts fall inside or outside it, need a Director ruling. The UPS and welfare readings are MIM editorial judgments from prisoner and staff authors. Nothing was modified, and no code or tests were run."
verifier_notes: All 30 findings were checked against sources. Local text and PDF quotes were matched after whitespace and entity normalization. Sakai chapters 4, 5, 6, 7 and 14 were fetched from readsettlers.org and matched. The Director ruling in ST-17 was verified against the verbatim entry in the user's memory file direction-ideology-sides-with-mim.md. No finding was dropped, because every cited quote exists. The 'corrected' verdicts narrow claims, mostly by removing uncited sub-claims. Specific corrections: ST-15 ('MIM Theory 1 and 10' became 'MIM's theory journals'); ST-23 ('important' became 'positive contribution'); ST-08 (the 'prisoner' attribution was removed); ST-24 (Rust settler concept narrowed, since community.bsl has a SETTLER community kind); and ST-17 (locator changed to the memory file). Unverified side details are not load-bearing. Examples are the Sakai Ch. II Bacon's Rebellion contrast, the MIM Theory 8 and 10 IWW citations, and the 1974 date in ST-14.

claim: MIM(Prisons)' glossary defines Amerikkka/Amerika as a nation, the white settler nation that has occupied North America since the 1600s. MIM Notes use 'settler nation' and 'settler masses' as a national category, with its own material interest, and not as a moral label for individuals.
game_relevance: The oppressor nation has to be a first-class dimension next to the oppressed nations. Today ADR171 names only Black, Chicano and Indigenous, so the settler nation needs a named or derived counterpart that the engine reads from cohort accounts and privileges, not from a flag.
tension: ADR171 names only oppressed nations. Adding an oppressor-nation dimension may need a Director check because it touches the reserved theory line and the nation overlap policy.

citations.quote: The white settler nation which has occupied North America since the 1600s.

citations.locator: MIM Notes 129 (1 Jan 1997), BayRAIL on Prop 209, line ~768
citations.quote: The white settler nation dominates oppressed nations within Amerikan borders just as imperialists reap the benefits of Third World labor

claim: MIM's labor-aristocracy thesis is the class content of the settler nation. The labor aristocracy is defined by earning more than the value of its labor. MIM holds that most white workers, including skilled workers and trade unionists, are not a revolutionary class because they reapportion surplus extracted from the Third World. The class position follows the account (wage versus value created), not the job title.
game_relevance: The default reading of a US wage-earning cohort is 'labor aristocracy' whenever its wage and benefits exceed the value its labor creates. That makes imperial-rent receipts and wage-versus-value accounting the test. A US wage cohort is not 'proletariat' by default.
tension: NORTH_STAR says households keep differences in income and ownership, and PER-337 forbids individual person agents. The reading must be computed per cohort, with some cohorts below the line (MIM treats lumpen, semi-proletarian and the poor as distinct). It also needs a Calibrated or Derived value-of-labor input that the repo may not have yet.

citations.quote: the labor aristocracy in the First World earn more than the value of their labor and therefore have interests that fall in the bourgeois camp allying with imperialism.

citations.locator: PDF p.35, Class Privilege and Oppression
citations.quote: They do not create surplus value as much as reapportion the surplus which results from super exploitation of the Third World.

claim: MIM states that the white labor aristocracy's turn to chauvinism has a material basis and is not a failure of leadership or education. MIM gives that basis as the reason an organizing line aimed at 'workers' in general does not work.
game_relevance: Consciousness or 'education' actions on a labor-aristocratic cohort should not shift it toward revolution while its balance stays positive. Its response is set by what it receives and risks losing. This matches the project's balance-sign finding and PER-337 (never infer agreement from aid).

citations.quote: For the ideology which leads white workers to seek more TVs instead of less capitalists has a material basis which is itself a barrier.

verification_note: Quote found on p.35. The source supports 'the ideology has a material basis which is itself a barrier'. The explicit contrasts ('not a failure of leadership or education') and 'reason an organizing line aimed at workers in general does not work' are the reader's paraphrase and are narrowed to what the quote says. Confidence lowered to medium.

claim: MIM's strategic frame is national alliances. Oppressor-nation people build class and gender alliances that use nationalism against the oppressed nations. The class alliance is labor aristocracy plus imperialist bourgeoisie, and the bourgeoisie generally leads it. The oppressed nations build revolutionary-nationalist alliances of the working masses with the left of the national bourgeoisie and part of the petty bourgeoisie.
game_relevance: Groups are not only classes. Each has a nation position, and the leadership of its alliance determines what it can demand. The engine can read 'who leads' from who controls the organization's budget, staff and agenda, including whether a bourgeois or aristocratic stratum holds the decisive accounts.

citations.quote: The people of the oppressor nations construct class and gender alliances that use nationalism to advance their class and gender interests within oppressor nations at the expense of the people of the oppressed nations.
In the oppressor nations, the bourgeoisie generally leads the national class alliance, and the patriarchy leads the national gender alliance.

claim: MIM(Prisons) edited the 1990 What's Your Line? text in 2011 to remove 'super exploitation of oppressed internal nations'. It now says exploitation of the oppressed nations is the exception in the US. The oppressed-nation penalty is therefore mainly exclusion, repression, imprisonment and lumpenization, not extraction of surplus from a big proletariat.
game_relevance: Oppressed-nation cohorts should not be modeled as the exploited proletariat of US capital by default. Their accounts should show barred access (credit, homeownership, hiring), policing and prison exposure, and a larger lumpen and semi-proletarian share. The 'bribe mass' versus 'deprivation mass' comparison in ADR171 fits this.
tension: The 1990 MIM text says the opposite. Where texts disagree, the later MIM(Prisons) edit is MIM's current line, but the Director has not confirmed that the later edit governs.

citations.locator: PDF p.35, preface to 'Class Privilege and Oppression'
citations.quote: Exploitation of the oppressed nations is the exception, not the rule in the United $tates.

claim: MIM adopted the settler analysis from Sakai's Settlers and distributed it widely. MIM credits Sakai for its analysis of the white working class as a non-revolutionary worker-elite. Sakai is an anarchist who criticizes Maoists in passing, and MIM calls the book 'mostly correct'. The history in Sakai is therefore MIM-endorsed evidence for the game, though not MIM-authored.
game_relevance: The dated cases below (ST-09 to ST-14) can be used as MIM-line history for scenario content. The FAQ's own words (not Sakai's) should be quoted wherever the game states an MIM position.

citations.quote: Since MIM developed its analysis of the white working class as a non-revolutionary worker-elite -- a labor aristocracy -- thanks to the work of J. Sakai
Sakai's book slams us Maoists in passing repeatedly, but it is mostly correct.

claim: Sakai ties the labor aristocracy to Engels and Lenin. It still does wage labor and grows out of the working class, but it is 'no longer exploited' because the bourgeoisie shares colonial superprofits with it. Sakai calls it the 'social base' of imperialism.
game_relevance: The mechanism is a transfer from the imperial bourgeoisie to a cohort stratum, which the engine can read as a flow in the cohort account. 'Prejudice' should not be a separate attitude stat. The cohort's loyalty is explained by what it receives and what it would lose.
tension: The no-fixed-response-curve rule means the 'social base' effect must come out of those flows, not a fixed response curve.

citations.quote: While the labor aristocracy engages in wage-labor and grows up out of the working class, it is no longer exploited.
just like the army or police (who are the military base of the imperialists, while the labor aristocracy is its social base)

verification_note: Both quotes found in fetched ch5. The sentence that racist politics under imperialism are 'an outward manifestation of a class alliance' was in the claim but had no citation and was not checked, so it was removed from the claim.

claim: MIM's pattern by case type: when white labor or a white-led left organization presses a demand, MIM asks where the increase comes from and who pays. In the 1997 UPS strike MIM Notes called the demand for more full-time jobs and pensions 'pie-hoarding' by the labor aristocracy. In 1994-95 white voters backing Republican welfare cuts were called a white nationalist movement that mistakes welfare for the poor for the real welfare for the rich and labor aristocracy.
game_relevance: A demand is classed by incidence: does it raise income for a labor-aristocratic cohort with the cost falling on periphery, oppressed-nation or lumpen cohorts, directly or through imperial rent? That is the 'bigger-slice' test in brief 06. It is a calculation over account changes with no label involved.
tension: The UPS article was written by a prisoner and MIM staff, and states a judgment, not a measurement. The engine should compute incidence and let the player see it, and not hard-code 'union strike = aristocratic'.

citations.locator: MIM Notes 145 (Sept 1997), 'UPS Workers Want Bigger Piece of Pie'
citations.quote: the settler nation working class is part of the Amerikan labor aristocracy and ceased to be defined as the proletariat specifically because the settler nation working class is not exploited

citations.locator: MIM Notes 96 (Jan 1995), 'Welfare, Crime and Immigration: White Nation Goes Bonkers'
citations.quote: The white nationalist movement has the distorted perception that the government is welfare for the poor instead of welfare for the rich and white labor aristocracy.

verification_note: Quotes found; 'pie- hoarding' appears in the UPS article's first sentence. Changed 'written by a prisoner and MIM staff' to 'by RC35 and MIM' because the source does not say prisoner. The Republican welfare-cuts framing is from the same MN96 article.

claim: Case 1, 1866-1869: the National Labor Union, the first major US white labor federation, defeated every motion to admit Black workers. Sakai reads the NLU's leaders as intending to push aside Afrikan labor. Who was excluded: Black workers. Who gained: white craft and immigrant workers.
game_relevance: Union and association membership can be an exclusion decision. The engine can record who a labor organization admits, whose jobs its demands reserve, and which cohorts' hiring or wage position falls as a result. Closed-shop and seniority-style demands show up as shifted labor supply.

citations.quote: All motions to admit Afrikans to the N.L.U. were defeated

verification_note: Quote found. Sakai writes the NLU leaders 'clearly intended to simply push aside Afrikan labor' and calls the NLU 'the first major labor federation of white workers'. The 'individual white unions barred them' and 'plan that used white labor to replace Black labor' wording was not verified verbatim and is narrowed to Sakai's 'push aside' reading.

claim: Case 2, 1877-1902: the white labor movement built itself against Chinese workers. The Working Men's Party of California (Kearney, late 1870s) ran on wiping out Chinese labor and won seats and control of the 1879 constitutional convention. After the 1882 Exclusion Act the Knights' Powderly said to 'finish the job'. Rock Springs miners killed more than 20 Chinese in 1885. Gompers co-authored a 1902 exclusion pamphlet. MIM adds that 99 percent of California white voters backed the 1879 ban. Who gained: white workers taking Chinese jobs and small businesses, and the party's leaders.
game_relevance: This is the template for a demand whose whole benefit is a transfer from a named group, here by immigration and border control. Electoral demands that restrict an outgroup's labor supply or residence raise white-cohort wages and are the clearest settler-demand signature in accounts: a gain to one cohort with a cost to a named, non-voting or minority cohort.

citations.locator: Ch. IV, section on 1882 Exclusion Act
citations.quote: the task for trade unionists was to finish the job - by eliminating all Chinese left in the U.S within the year!
the infamous Rock Springs, Wyoming massacre took place, where over 20 Chinese miners were killed by a storm of rifle-fire
In 1879, 99% of California white voters voted to ban Chinese immigration

claim: Case 3, 1840s onward: the white workers' movement's main slogan was 'Vote Yourself A Farm', a demand for cheap land. Sakai reads it as a claim on settler land, which means the dispossession of Indigenous nations. MIM's 1992 piece adds that poor whites demanded 'total subjugation' of native peoples, and the Bacon's Rebellion tradition of 1676. Who paid: Indigenous nations. Who gained: white farmers and craftsmen.
game_relevance: Land access is the first thing a settler demand leaves intact or enlarges. The engine can score a demand by whether it assigns land or housing and whose recorded territory or claim it comes from, since geography is fixed and political claims are overlays. A program that raises household welfare through land taken from a named nation shows the cost in that nation's claim account.
tension: Sakai (Ch. II) and MIM (MN69) read Bacon's Rebellion differently: Sakai says Black slaves also fought in it, while MIM stresses the white farmers' demand to destroy native peoples. The game should not hard-code a single reading of that event.

citations.quote: The dominant political slogan of the white workers movement of the 1840's was "Vote Yourself A Farm".
white farmers led a revolt (Bacon's rebellion) to demand more land-grabbing war on native people

claim: Case 4, 1905-1920, a counter-case: Sakai calls the IWW the last white union movement to be socialist and internationalist. It was based on the most exploited white workers, and declared that industrial unionism meant including Mexicanos, Asians, Afrikans and Indians.
game_relevance: The engine should not treat 'white labor' as one case. An organization of poor and migrant white workers that includes oppressed-nation members and has no claim on land or border privilege should read as non-settler in its accounts. Settlerness depends on what the organization's demands do and who is admitted, not on the share of white members.
tension: Sakai's IWW is a Sakai (anarchist) judgment. MIM(Prisons) cites the IWW only through MIM Theory 8 and 10, which are not available locally.

citations.quote: explicitly declaring that industrial unionism meant the inclusion of Mexicanos, Asians, Afrikans, Indians and all nationalities.
the I.W.W. was the last white union movement to be socialist, it also represented the last stratum of white workers to be in any way internationalist.

verification_note: Both quotes found. Sakai's passage begins 'the usual settler trade-unionism characterized the I.W.W.' so the claim that the IWW had 'no gain for the settler order' and 'urged rejecting loyalty to the US' / 'crushed' were not verified and were dropped from the claim; the tension now flags Sakai's own settler-unionism label.

claim: Case 5, 1936-1937 CIO: after the Flint sit-down GM gave in. Sakai says the victory 'firm positioned' the Euro-Amerikan working class in the settler ranks and that the New Deal gave European 'ethnic' minorities integration as Amerikans by raising their privileges. Only five Black workers took part in Flint and three at Dodge Main. Flint organizer Bob Travis, a Communist Party leader, reported total elimination of wildcat actions to observe the contract.
game_relevance: A real class victory (higher wages, stronger union) can still be a settler gain. The engine can show both, a wage rise for the cohort and an unchanged or worse position for oppressed-nation cohorts, and show 'integration' of immigrant cohorts as a bundle of privileges conferred. A union that polices its own wildcats for a contract is an organization turning into an institution that holds a stake.
tension: Sakai is a hostile reader of the CIO and the CPUSA. MIM's own 1990 review calls the CPUSA's 1930s CIO work an 'actual gain' and praises its organization, so MIM is not uniformly negative about it. The game should show both readings.

citations.quote: The victory they gained was the firm positioning of the Euro-Amerikan working class in the settler ranks
Only five Afrikans took part in the Flint Sit-Down Strike.
in the total elimination of wild-cat actions during the past 3 months.
the Communist Party of the 1930s accomplished what it did in putting together the CIO and the whole deal for labor at the time

verification_note: All quotes found; 90-day GM 'gave in' and Dodge Main 'only three' confirmed. Removed the claim that Black and Mexican workers were 'struck down' (not verified) and the attribution to 'CPUSA organizers' in plural: Sakai names Travis only. MIM's 'actual gains' phrase is in the same review; 'praises its organization' is the reader's gloss.

claim: Case 6, 1974: in Alabama the Revolutionary Union, the October League and the Black Workers Congress, among others, allied with the United Mine Workers around a South African coal boycott. When District 20 asked the Afrikan dockworkers in Mobile to refuse to unload the coal, they refused, and Sakai says the scheme blew apart because the UMW district leadership was reactionary and white-supremacist.
game_relevance: A rival organization's tactical 'unity' can be tested by whether the oppressed-nation side joins it on its own terms. The engine can compare what the white-led bloc claims to offer with what the oppressed-nation cohort chooses when it has its own organization to join. Refusal is a result of material interest and is not scripted.
tension: RU and OL are opposed-line organizations in the Director's ruling. Sakai's account of them is a rival's account, and this finding only describes the pattern.

citations.quote: It turned out that the UMW District 20 leadership was, of course, totally reactionary and white-supremacist.

verification_note: Quote and Mobile dockworkers episode confirmed. Sakai says the UMW only wanted to boycott foreign coal 'to save settler jobs'. The year 1974 and 'left press hailed' were not checked in the fetched text; 'Black Workers Congress' is listed among the organizations by Sakai. Wording tightened to what Sakai states.

claim: MIM's 1996-97 account of a conference fight with FRSO and an imperialist-country activist. They said 'workers of the world should unite, not divide' and called MIM's position unscientific. MIM answers that this unity is on the labor aristocracy's terms. MIM adds that the FRSO activist admitted he had not read MIM's theory journals on the subject.
game_relevance: This is the 'settler communist' offer in MIM's words, for a rival organization inside the game: class unity that treats the labor aristocracy as part of the proletariat and so leaves the superwage arrangement intact. It attracts cohorts whose accounts gain from that arrangement. The engine judges FRSO-type groups by what their programs do to those accounts, as it judges every group.
tension: This is MIM's polemic about a rival and is not neutral. The Director's ruling (MCU and FRSO as settler communist organizations opposed to MIM) has no further text in the corpus beyond this polemic.

citations.quote: the kind of unity the critics were advocating is the kind where the proletarians unite with the labor aristocracy on the latter's terms. No thanks!
an activist from the U.S.-based Freedom Road Socialist Organization (FRSO), who repeated the first critic's comment and added that MIM's position is unscientific

verification_note: Quotes found. The original claim said the FRSO activist had not read 'MIM Theory 1 and 10'; the source says only 'MIM's theory journals on the subject' (a footnote separately cites MIM Theory 10). Corrected. 'workers of the world should unite, not divide' also found in mn129.

claim: An MCU text, which is opposed-line evidence, defines the labor aristocracy as 'only a small subsection of the working class', not equal to union membership as a whole, and says its bribery peaked in the New Deal era and has eroded since the mid-1970s. A second MCU text lists whether the US is a settler-colonial country as an open study question. MIM says the majority of white workers are labor aristocrats.
game_relevance: This shows what a rival line in the game says and what it recruits: workers who reject the 'mostly bribed' reading and want the union movement treated as the base. It is an opposed-line practice. MCU's text must not be used for any engine rule on class or union work (Director ruling 2).
tension: MIM: 'majority of white workers' (FPLmimp p.35) versus MCU: a 'small subsection'. The game follows MIM, and MCU's figure is not an input. This sits as in-game rival belief only.

citations.locator: PDF p.3, thesis on the labor aristocracy
citations.quote: the labor aristocracy which is only a small subsection of the working class, and in our day is not equivalent to the trade union membership as a whole.
if the U.S. is currently a settler-colonial country

source_standing: OPPOSED LINE (MCU): by Director ruling, settler communist and opposed to the MIM line. Evidence of what that line says or does; never support for the game's own method.

claim: Director ruling relayed 18 Nov 2026: MCU and FRSO are settler communist organizations opposed to the MIM line. The ruling is binding for this research and the design. The game identifies them as rival organizations, and engine judgment is still by material accounts.
game_relevance: Rival organizations in the game can carry these descriptions in their dossiers. The engine does not read the label. It reads what the organization demands, whom it admits, whose accounts it improves and what it leaves intact.

citations.quote: MCU and FRSO are both settler communist organizations opposed to the MIM line

verification_note: Verbatim quote found in the Director-ruling memory note (dated 2026-11-18). Locator changed from 'relayed in task' to that memory file.

claim: MIM's stated test for a movement inside the US is whether it opposes Amerika fundamentally or only 'poses left' while seeking a unified oppressor nation. MIM adds that the only revolutionary movement within Amerika since 1492 is the movement of the oppressed nations against the dominant nation, and that no working class or feminist movement is revolutionary without adopting the oppressed nations' perspective.
game_relevance: The test is relational. A group is settler-leaning when its program unifies the oppressor nation at the oppressed nations' cost, and anti-imperialist when its program is led by and answers to the oppressed nations. The engine can implement this as 'whose demands come first and whose accounts pay', not a membership count.

citations.quote: does the movement fundamentally oppose Amerika and all that it stands for? Or does it merely pose left in its quest -- deliberate or accidental -- for a unified oppressor nation?
The only revolutionary movement within Amerika since 1492 been the movement of oppressed nations against the dominant Amerikan nation.

claim: Sakai gives a second test, about alliances. He argues that 'correct alliances must be based on correct strategy' and that the Euro-Amerikan labor aristocracy uses tactical unity to protect settler privilege and hegemony over labor.
game_relevance: Cross-nation union membership is not a stepping stone to revolutionary unity by default. The engine can track whether a mixed organization's gains come from shared work or from one nation's group holding the decisive positions, and let an oppressed-nation cohort leave a mixed body for its own.
tension: This is Sakai's argument, which MIM calls 'mostly correct'. MIM's own union policy is not in the texts I read, and MCU and FRSO union work is opposed-line practice here.

citations.quote: Correct alliances must be based on correct strategy.

the Euro-Amerikan labor aristocracy uses tactical unity and the surface appearance of advancing the common good, but only really acts to protect settler privilege and maintain settler hegemony over labor.

verification_note: Both quotes found. The strategic-versus-tactical-unity taxonomy and 'money-based' wording were not verified verbatim and were removed from the claim.

claim: What the settler arrangement leaves intact, by MIM's accounts. Land: settler holidays and 'mythology' cover the theft (MN153). Superwages: 'more TVs instead of less capitalists' (FPL), pensions and full-time jobs (UPS, MN145). Borders and labor supply: the 'Made with White Labor Only' boycotts and 'keep immigrant competition away' (MN69). Police and prisons: the rest of the oppressor nation backs the job-security plans of police and correctional officers to protect collective privilege, and prison jobs offer cushy exploiter wages (FPLmimp p.37-38).
game_relevance: The four items (land, superwage, borders, police) give four checks the engine can compute from accounts: does the program change land claims, the wage-versus-value gap, the labor-supply restriction on a named group, or the share of public budget going to enforcement jobs that cohorts rely on? A program that raises incomes while leaving all four unchanged is the settler form.

citations.quote: the rest of the oppressor nation is willing to go along with the job security plans of the police and correctional officers as a means of protecting their collective privilege.
What a beefed-up injustice system does offer economically is a means of employing millions of people at cushy exploiter wages.
white workers forced their unions to organize boycotts of goods which were not "Made with White Labor Only."

claim: MIM's account of what oppressed-nation organizations do differently: they build independent institutions and an anti-imperialist united front instead of relying on imperialist elections or white allies. MIM praises Indigenous groups that make land and territory central and call for economic self-sufficiency. Sakai's League of Revolutionary Black Workers (1967 onward) organized Black auto workers against the UAW and was attacked by its leadership and by police.
game_relevance: Oppressed-nation cohorts should have organization choices of their own, including organizations that build independent institutions (media, mutual aid, land use) and decline settler-led bodies. Land and territory belong to the demand set, and the engine should track whether an organization's offer rises or falls when the settler-led alternative is present.

citations.locator: MIM Notes 129, BayRAIL on Prop 209, lines ~788-791
citations.quote: The oppressed need to build independent institutions and strengthen the anti-imperialist United Front in order to kick the oppressors out and seize state power.
They identify land and territory as central to the struggle for national liberation, and call for economic self-sufficiency.

citations.locator: Ch. XIV, League of Revolutionary Black Workers
citations.quote: The League represented the militant, anti-capitalist and anti-settler union sentiment of the young Afrikan workers in the Detroit auto plants.

claim: MIM does not treat oppressed-nation membership as a guarantee. MIM(Prisons) says NAMP organized New Afrikans 'benefiting from imperialism' around a bigger piece of the pie, which it calls the most common line among New Afrikan nationalist organizations, and says it tries to unite the national bourgeoisies behind smashing imperialism, 'cautiously'. It calls cultural nationalism and integrationism enemy ideologies tending toward fascism.
game_relevance: An oppressed-nation organization can fail the same test: a 'bigger slice' program led by a national bourgeois or petty-bourgeois stratum. The 'comprador' flip in brief 06 covers this. The engine should apply the one incidence test to organizations of every nation.
tension: MIM uses 'cautiously' for the national bourgeoisie, so national-bourgeois cohorts need a conditional ally status and not a fixed enemy or friend status.

citations.quote: telling New Afrikans benefiting from imperialism that they deserved a bigger piece of the pie.
We cautiously attempt to unite the national bourgeoisies of the oppressed nationalities behind the program of smashing imperialism.

claim: MIM reviews Ignatiev's How the Irish Became White (MIM Notes 107, Dec 1995, review by MC5) as 'a positive contribution to white labor history', though 'not as clear theoretically as Sakai'. Sakai's New Deal account says the New Deal gave European 'ethnic' minorities integration as Amerikans by raising their privileges. Membership in the settler nation is therefore conferred through privileges and acceptance, and is not fixed by descent.
game_relevance: A cohort's nation position can change over time as it gains or loses the privileges that make it part of the oppressor nation. This needs cohort-level accounts of access (jobs, credit, housing, policing) over many periods, not a stored label.
tension: MIM's 'nation' category is not a settled map to census categories. ADR171 handles overlaps for oppressed nations only.

citations.quote: Ignatiev's book is a positive contribution to white labor history which serves MIM in a timely way

citations.locator: Ch. VII, section 3 'New Deal & Class Struggle'
citations.quote: It gave the European "ethnic" national minorities real integration as Amerikans by sharply raising their privileges.

verification_note: Quotes found. Changed 'important contribution' to the source's 'positive contribution' and added MIM's caveat that Ignatiev is less clear theoretically than Sakai. The 'conferred not fixed by descent' conclusion is the reader's inference from two sources, not an MIM statement.

claim: The repo's research brief 24 settles the 'red-settler trap' as a design rule. A socialism that leaves land and extraction intact has left the founding act in place, and the trap detector RED_SETTLER_TRAP_DETECTED fires on 'the ruling faction's own' high class_reduction with a non-ABOLISH material record. The Python-era balkanization spec tags factions with is_settler_formation as a property of the base. In the Rust tree, 'settler' appears only in territory.bsl, community.bsl (a SETTLER community kind) and the community conformance test.
game_relevance: The design direction (settlerness is read from material record) agrees with MIM, but the live Rust campaign has none of the faction-level trap or is_settler_formation. A class-agent design would have to compute the 'non-ABOLISH record' from accounts, such as land claims and extraction by nation.
tension: Brief 24 is research, not a binding ruling. The balkanization spec lives under the Python era and is not live authority. Do not infer authority from old ADRs.

citations.quote: that accumulation intact has left the founding act of its own working class intact.
Does this faction's base come from the settler population?

verification_note: Both quotes and 'ruling faction's own high class_reduction' found. A rg of .bsl/.rs files lists territory.bsl, community.bsl and community_conformance.rs mentioning 'settler', and community.bsl does contain CommunityType/SETTLER, so 'no settler concept' was narrowed. The 'sovereignty layer inert in the Python bridge' memory note was not re-verified here and is removed from the claim.

claim: Brief 06 already holds computable flip rules for the pattern. 'Bigger-slice' (rule 3) says an organization adopts a demand whose incidence falls only on the core, with the test 'does it name the periphery?' and the symptom 'popular, and the state does not oppose it'. A rule 8 covers national-bourgeois leadership converting national grievance into a claim on Phi (the 'comprador' pattern).
game_relevance: These rules map to the settler pattern in ST-08 to ST-22. They need an incidence calculation (who gains, who pays) that class-agent choices can feed. The 'state does not oppose it' symptom is a usable observable.

citations.quote: adopts a demand whose incidence falls only on the core.
national-bourgeois leadership converts national grievance into a claim on Φ.

verification_note: Both quotes found and the 'popular, and the state does not oppose it' symptom is at line 314. The 'Fascist' flip rule (white-lumpen grievance into national identity) was not re-checked and is removed from the claim.

claim: Brief 21 names the Strasserite/patsoc grifter as a rival whose own objective is 'respectability inside the settler nation', who recruits from the labor aristocracy and small business, and whose tell is 'class unity that never names a class relation'. ADR054 (Python era) has chauvinism accrue on organization-to-member edges and rolls 'sigmoid(chi - discipline)' on crisis events.
game_relevance: Rival organizations that mimic the left while serving settler interest already have a dossier shape (mandate, target class, tell). The tell 'never names a class relation' is checkable against the program's incidence.
tension: ADR054's sigmoid roll as a mechanism conflicts with the constitutional rule 'no imposed sigmoid or second fixed response curve'. It should not be carried into the Rust design.

claim: Proposal: derive 'settler pattern' per organization from a demand-incidence record, with no 'is_settler' label. For each demand or program an organization advances, compute (a) the change in each cohort's wage-versus-value gap and income, (b) the cost carried by named oppressed-nation, periphery or lumpen cohorts, directly or through imperial rent, land claims, labor-supply restriction or enforcement budget, and (c) who holds the leading positions. The pattern appears when gains are concentrated in labor-aristocratic cohorts and the cost falls on others.
game_relevance: Each period, population groups choosing among organizations see an offer with a computed gain to them and an observable cost to others. The player sees a settler pattern as a result they can read off accounts, and the engine's judgment stays material. Groups choose by their own accounts, and no political label scripts success or failure.
tension: It needs a Derived value-of-labor and imperial-rent allocation by cohort, which may not exist in the live campaign. It must also respect 'never infer political consciousness from aid or provisioning' (PER-337), so the choice rule uses the offer's effect on accounts and not a consciousness variable.

claim: Proposal: what an organization 'must give up' to count as anti-imperialist is also computable. Under MIM's test, a program does not leave the four items intact: land claims move toward the named nation, the wage-versus-value gap of aristocratic cohorts narrows, restrictions on a named group's labor supply fall, and enforcement jobs shrink. Each is a cost that cohorts with those gains will see, so the engine should show the player which cohorts leave when the program takes that step.
game_relevance: The player's political choices become a trade-off visible in accounts: a program that serves oppressed-nation cohorts loses some aristocratic membership, and a program that holds aristocratic membership leaves land, wages, borders and police intact. Neither outcome is scripted, and a revolutionary, reformist or electoral project can each be tried.
tension: MIM's line would say the first path leads to a smaller but more reliable base. The game must not turn that into a fixed rule that the aristocratic path always fails. Outcomes are judged from accounts, and MIM's claim that the electoral route cannot reach the imperial flow is a hypothesis the engine tests, not a given.

citations.quote: The oppressed cannot expect to make real gains by participating in the imperialist's elections.

claim: Proposal on elections: a settler-pattern electorate shows up as a bloc vote whose measured gain falls on a named group. MIM Notes 96 (citing USA Today) says the Republican Party took 63 percent of the white male vote in the 1994 Congressional elections, attracted by blaming other peoples for crime, welfare and immigration. An election in the game can change who holds office and public budgets, but a program that needs oppressed-nation cohorts' cost to stay in place will win white-cohort votes while the engine records the cost.
game_relevance: Who can vote and what an office decides (NORTH_STAR) are the engine inputs. An election can move budget lines such as enforcement, welfare and immigration restriction. MIM's line implies it cannot by itself change the imperial flow or land, which the engine can test by whether those accounts move after a win.
tension: The 63 percent figure is MIM's reading of a USA Today poll in a 1995 issue and is not in the repo's data. 'Elections cannot reach the imperial flow' is MIM's claim and not a verified engine result.

claim: MIM Notes 153 treats police as the enforcement arm of the settler nation: 'Amerikkkan police serve to protect the white settler nation', which has a material interest in suppressing indigenous history. It also treats the settler holiday and its mythology as covering the theft, and the settler-imperialist relationship as the basis of prisons.
game_relevance: Police and public-order spending belongs to the state organization's side of the incidence record, and who benefits from enforcement spending can be read from the county budget and the cohorts employed or protected by it. The relation between police and an oppressed-nation cohort is a cost that the engine can show.
